intro.en: Deception is the Latin noun deceptio, from decipere, to catch in a trap.
intro.cn: deception 就是拉丁名词 deceptio，来自 decipere（设套捕捉）。

items.en: Deceptio named the act of catching someone in a trap.
items.cn: deceptio 指把人套住的行为。

items.en: The trap became a trick of words and appearances.
items.cn: 捕兽的套子变成了言语与外表上的圈套。

items.en: Déception meant a betrayal of trust.
items.cn: déception 指对信任的背弃。

items.en: Deception entered English as the noun of deceive.
items.cn: deception 作为 deceive 的名词进入英语。

items.en: It now covers lies, disguises and optical tricks.
items.cn: 如今它涵盖谎言、伪装与视觉把戏。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -ception ending, and the meaning group names kinds of dishonesty.
note.cn: 形近组共享 -ception 结尾，近义组则列出各种不诚实。

definition_zh: 相像的；相似的；同样地；一视同仁地
definition_en: similar in appearance or character, or in the same manner
core_image: 两只并排摆着的白瓷杯，形状、花纹与缺口几乎一模一样
scene: 双胞胎姐妹穿着一模一样的校服走进礼堂，连班主任都愣了一下。 The twins looked so alike that even their teachers confused them.
sceneCN: 这里的 alike 是「相像的」（第 1 个义项：外观或性质相似）；句意是这对双胞胎长得太像，连老师都会认错。

pos.zh: 形容词：相像的；相似的（多作表语）
副词：同样地；一视同仁地

derivatives.zh: 同源词，义为「像；如同」，也可作动词「喜欢」
由 like 加名词后缀构成，义为「相似；肖像」
由 like 加 -wise 构成，义为「同样地；此外」
由 un- 加 like 构成，义为「不像；与……不同」
由 alike 加 -ness 构成，义为「相似之处」，使用频率较低

senses.title: Similar to each other
senses.definition: similar to one another in appearance, character, or amount, used mainly after a linking verb
senses.definitionCN: 在外观、性格或数量上彼此相似，主要用在系动词之后作表语
senses.example: The two brothers look very much alike.
senses.exampleCN: 这两兄弟长得非常像。
senses.why: Old English gelic was built from lic, the word for 'body or form'; alike therefore says that two things share one form, and the sense survives in the predicative pattern look alike.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 gelic 由 lic「身体、形体」构成，alike 本义就是「共有一个形体」；这一层意思保留在 look alike 这类表语用法里，所以它几乎不作定语放在名词前。

senses.title: In the same way
senses.definition: in the same manner, or equally, with no difference in treatment
senses.definitionCN: 以相同的方式，或平等地、不加区别地对待
senses.example: The law applies alike to citizens and to visitors.
senses.exampleCN: 法律对本国公民和外来访客同样适用。
senses.why: The adverb is the adjective turned into a manner word: if two parties are alike in standing, they are treated alike, and the -ly form never developed because the old form already ended in a suffix.
senses.whyCN: 副词义是把形容词转成方式状语：如果两方地位相像，就会被同样对待。英语里没有再造出 alikely，因为 alike 本身已经带后缀，直接兼作副词。

intro.en: Alike is a Germanic compound whose second half once meant 'body', so the word began as a statement about shared form.
intro.cn: alike 是日耳曼语复合词，后半部分原义为「身体、形体」，因此这个词最初说的是「共有一个形体」。

items.en: *galaikaz is reconstructed as 'having the same form', built from the prefix *ga- and *laikaz 'body, form'.
items.cn: 原始日耳曼语 *galaikaz 一般重构为「具有相同形体」，由前缀 *ga- 与 *laikaz「身体、形体」构成。

items.en: Old English gelic and the variant onlic carried the sense 'like, similar' and were already used after verbs such as beon.
items.cn: 古英语 gelic 及其变体 onlic 表示「相像的」，当时就常放在 beon 这类动词之后使用。

items.en: In Middle English the form ilike appears; the initial vowel was later remade as a-, giving alike by the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 中古英语出现 ilike 这一形式，词首元音后来改作 a-，到十六世纪定型为 alike。

items.en: The word settled into predicative use: two things are alike, but one does not normally speak of an alike pair.
items.cn: 这个词固定用于表语位置：可以说两样东西 are alike，但一般不说 an alike pair。

items.en: The phrase young and old alike generalises the adverb sense into 'everyone, without distinction'.
items.cn: young and old alike 这一说法把副词义扩展为「所有人，不加区别」。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Germanic root for 'form'; the near-meaning group gathers words of similarity and sameness with different grammar.
note.cn: 形近组共享表示「形体」的日耳曼词根；近义组收表示相似与相同的词，语法用法各不相同。

normal.en: The stress is on the first syllable: BAL-co-ny.
normal.cn: 重音在第一音节。

normal.en: A balcony has a rail so people do not fall.
normal.cn: 阳台有栏杆，防止人跌落。

normal.en: Theatre balconies are the upper seats.
normal.cn: 剧院的 balcony 是楼上座位。

normal.en: A small balcony can be called a balconette.
normal.cn: 小阳台可以叫 balconette。

abstract.en: See a window opening onto iron rails.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇窗推开通向铁栏杆。

abstract.en: See a potted plant against the sky.
abstract.cn: 想象一盆植物衬着天空。

abstract.en: See a row of seats high above a stage.
abstract.cn: 想象舞台上方的一排座位。

examples.en: She stood on the balcony and watched the street.
examples.cn: 她站在阳台上看街。

examples.en: We watched the play from the upper balcony.
examples.cn: 我们在楼上楼厅看戏。

examples.en: He put two chairs on the balcony.
examples.cn: 他在阳台上放了两把椅子。

dict_mnemonic.text: bal-cony 像「栏杆围出的小天地」：窗外那一方带栏杆的平台，就是 balcony。

root: 源自意大利语 balcone「脚手架」，更早来自 balco「横梁」，经法语 balcon 进入英语；由架高的平台引申为楼房阳台，再指剧院楼座。

sensesIntro.en: The outdoor platform and the upper theatre seats are both raised places to stand or sit.
sensesIntro.cn: 户外平台与剧院楼座，都是架高起来供人站立或就座的地方。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a window opening onto iron rails.
core.cn: 核心意象：一扇窗推开通向铁栏杆。

branches.en: on the balcony
branches.cn: 在阳台上

branches.en: a balcony view
branches.cn: 阳台景色

branches.en: step onto the balcony
branches.cn: 走到阳台上

branches.en: the upper balcony
branches.cn: 楼上楼厅

branches.en: balcony seats
branches.cn: 楼座票

intro.en: The -ed suffix gives balconied, meaning having a balcony.
intro.cn: 后缀 -ed 构成 balconied，义为「有阳台的」。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin base; the word came through Italian and French.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁词基，这个词经意大利语与法语传来。

definition_zh: （战争、灾难等的）后果；余波；（农业）再生草
definition_en: the situation or consequences left after a damaging event, or in farming, a second crop of grass grown after mowing
core_image: 洪水退去的街道上，泥浆、断枝和倒下的招牌摊了一地
scene: 风暴过去两天，渔港的水面仍漂着碎木板。 The village is still clearing up the aftermath of the flood.
sceneCN: 这里的 aftermath 是「后果、余波」（第 1 个义项：灾祸之后留下的局面）；句意是村子仍在清理洪水留下的残局。

derivatives.zh: 复合词的前半部分，义为「在……之后」
复数形式，义为「多次灾祸的余波」

senses.title: The consequences of a damaging event
senses.definition: the situation that remains after a war, disaster, or other damaging event
senses.definitionCN: 战争、灾难或其他破坏性事件之后留下的局面
senses.example: The village is still clearing up the aftermath of the flood.
senses.exampleCN: 村子仍在清理洪水留下的残局。
senses.why: The word first meant grass cut after the main harvest; that second cutting became a picture of what grows or remains after the main event.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指主收割之后割下的一茬草；这「第二茬」逐渐成了主事件之后长出的、留下之物的图景。

senses.title: A second crop of grass
senses.definition: in farming, grass that grows again after a field has been mown
senses.definitionCN: 农耕中，田地割过之后重新长出的草
senses.example: The farmer cut the aftermath for hay in late summer.
senses.exampleCN: 农夫在夏末把再生草割下做干草。
senses.why: This is the original sense, still used in agriculture: the crop that follows the first cutting of a field.
senses.whyCN: 这是最初的本义，农业中仍在使用：一块田第一次割过之后又收的那一茬。

intro.en: An old farming word about a second mowing, which became a word for what follows a disaster.
intro.cn: 一个关于「第二茬割草」的古老农事词，后来变成指灾后遗留局面的词。

items.en: mæth meant a mowing or a crop of grass, related to the verb mawan, to mow.
items.cn: mæth 意为「割草、一茬草」，与动词 mawan「割」同源。

items.en: æfter meant after or behind, and was freely joined to nouns to mark what comes later.
items.cn: æfter 意为「在……之后、在后」，常与名词组合以标记较晚的一方。

items.en: aftermath named the grass that grew after the first mowing was taken.
items.cn: aftermath 指第一次割草收走之后又长出的草。

items.en: Writers began using the word figuratively for any second growth or consequence.
items.cn: 十六世纪起，作家开始把这个词比喻地用于任何「后续的生长」或后果。

items.en: In modern use the figurative sense dominates, almost always in the pattern in the aftermath of something bad.
items.cn: 现代用法中比喻义占主导，几乎总出现在 in the aftermath of 某个坏事的句框里。

note.en: The first group shares the after- element; the second gathers words for consequences and destruction.
note.cn: 第一组共享 after- 成分；第二组收表示「后果」与「破坏」的词。

entries.definition: later than, or behind
the part of the day after noon
at a later time
mathematics in American English; here the old element meant mowing
entries.definitionCN: 美式口语的「数学」；在此词里旧义是「割草」

entries.definition: a result of an action or event
the bad results that follow an event
the track left behind by something moving, used figuratively
what happens because of something else

normalIntro.en: The -math here is old for mowing: the aftermath is the grass after the cut.
normalIntro.cn: 这里的 -math 是古语「割草」：aftermath 就是割过之后又长的草。

normal.en: Think of math as mowing here, not arithmetic.
normal.cn: 这里的 math 要理解成「割草」，不是算术。

normal.en: The literal aftermath is the second crop of hay.
normal.cn: 字面的 aftermath 是第二茬干草。

normal.en: The figurative aftermath is what is left after a disaster.
normal.cn: 比喻义的 aftermath 是灾难之后留下的东西。

normal.en: The common frame is in the aftermath of an event.
normal.cn: 常见句框是 in the aftermath of 某个事件。

normal.en: Spell it as after plus math, with no hyphen.
normal.cn: 拼写就是 after 加 math，中间不加连字符。

abstract.en: Picture a field just mown, with short green shoots already pushing up.
abstract.cn: 想象刚割过的田里，短短的新绿已经冒头。

abstract.en: See the same field after a flood, covered in mud instead of grass.
abstract.cn: 想象同一块田被洪水淹过，铺满泥浆而非青草。

abstract.en: Imagine a second growth of any kind: grass, rubble, or rumour.
abstract.cn: 想象任何一种「第二茬」：青草、瓦砾或流言。

examples.en: Hospitals struggled in the aftermath of the earthquake.
examples.cn: 地震之后，医院在余波中艰难运转。

examples.en: The government faced criticism in the immediate aftermath of the vote.
examples.cn: 投票刚结束的那段时间，政府就面临批评。

examples.en: The farmer sold the aftermath as winter feed.
examples.cn: 农夫把再生草当作冬季饲料卖掉。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿夫特马思」——阿夫特事后才慢慢思量，风暴过后满地狼藉。

root: 古英语 æfter「在后」与 mæth「割草、一茬草」合成 aftermath，本指第一次割草后重生的第二茬；十六世纪起引申为任何事件之后留下的局面。

sensesIntro.en: The literal sense is a second crop of grass; the figurative sense is the second growth of a disaster.
sensesIntro.cn: 字面义是第二茬青草，比喻义是灾难之后长出的「第二茬」局面。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a freshly mown field with new green shoots pushing up.
core.cn: 核心意象：刚割过的田里冒出新绿。

branches.en: a fishing port clearing storm debris
branches.cn: 清理风暴残骸的渔港

branches.en: hospitals coping after an earthquake
branches.cn: 地震之后苦苦支撑的医院

branches.en: a second crop cut for winter hay
branches.cn: 割下作冬饲料的第二茬草

branches.en: the weeks just after a vote
branches.cn: 投票刚结束的那几周

branches.en: grass after the scythe, rubble after the storm
branches.cn: 镰刀之后的草，风暴之后的瓦砾

intro.en: Two Old English pieces, after and mowing, joined into one noun.
intro.cn: 两个古英语部件「在后」与「割草」合成了一个名词。

latinIntro.en: Both elements are Germanic, so no Latin entries are listed.
latinIntro.cn: 两个部件都属日耳曼语，因此这里不列拉丁词条。

items.meaning: a mowing, a crop of grass

definition_zh: 相对性；相对论
definition_en: the quality of being true only in relation to something else; the physical theory that space, time, and motion depend on the observer
core_image: 两列火车交错而过，月台上的人与车上的人各看到不同的运动
scene: 两列火车在站台两侧交错而过，车上的人觉得自己不动，站台上的人却看到一切在飞驰。 Einstein's theory of relativity changed how we think about time.
sceneCN: 这里 relativity 是「相对论」（第 2 个义项：关于时空与运动依赖观察者的物理理论）；句意为爱因斯坦的相对论改变了我们对时间的看法。画面里可留意：交错而过的两列火车、站台上的人。

derivatives.zh: 相对的
相对地
相对主义者

senses.title: The state of being relative
senses.definition: the condition of being true or meaningful only in relation to something else
senses.definitionCN: 只有相对于其他事物才成立或有意义的状态
senses.example: The relativity of taste makes arguments about food endless.
senses.exampleCN: 口味的相对性让关于食物的争论没有尽头。
senses.why: The noun names the condition the adjective describes: a judgement with no fixed frame outside itself.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词命名形容词所描述的状态：一个没有外部固定坐标的判断。

senses.title: The physical theory
senses.definition: the theory that measurements of space, time, and motion depend on the observer's frame
senses.definitionCN: 认为空间、时间与运动的测量依赖观察者参考系的理论
senses.example: Einstein's theory of relativity changed how we think about time.
senses.exampleCN: 爱因斯坦的相对论改变了我们对时间的看法。
senses.why: Physics took the ordinary idea of relative measurement and made it a law: even time is measured against a frame.
senses.whyCN: 物理学把日常的「相对测量」观念变成定律：连时间也是相对于某个参考系来测量的。

intro.en: Relativity is the noun of relative: first a general condition of comparison, then the name of a physical theory.
intro.cn: relativity 是 relative 的名词：先指一般的比较状态，后成为一个物理理论的名称。

items.en: Relatus meant carried back, and a quantity carried back to another is measured relatively.
items.cn: relatus 意为被带回的，一个量被带回另一个量那里，就是以相对方式测量。

items.en: Relativus meant having relation to something else, the source of the adjective.
items.cn: relativus 意为与其他事物有关的，是形容词的来源。

items.en: English relative described what holds only in comparison with something else.
items.cn: 英语 relative 描述只在与其他事物比较中成立的东西。

items.en: The ending -ity made a noun of that quality, and relativity named the condition itself.
items.cn: 词尾 -ity 把这种性质变成名词，relativity 便命名这一状态本身。

items.en: In the twentieth century the word became the name of the theory that measurement depends on the observer.
items.cn: 在二十世纪，这个词成为「测量依赖观察者」这一理论的名称。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words of the same comparison family; the near-meaning group gathers terms about frames and conditions.
note.cn: 形近组收同一比较词族的词；近义组收关于参考系与条件性的词。

entries.definition: Compared, not absolute.

normalIntro.en: The noun starts as a habit of mind, measuring one thing against another, and ends as a law of physics.
normalIntro.cn: 这个名词从一种思维习惯开始——以一物量另一物——最后成为一条物理定律。

normal.en: Relative plus ity: the state of being measured against something.
normal.cn: relative 加 ity：以某物为参照来衡量这种状态。

normal.en: General relativity deals with gravity; special relativity with speed.
normal.cn: general relativity 讲引力，special relativity 讲速度。

normal.en: Cultural relativity says a custom must be judged in its own setting.
normal.cn: cultural relativity 认为一种习俗须在其自身环境中评判。

normal.en: The theory keeps the everyday word and makes it exact.
normal.cn: 这个理论保留了日常的词，却把它变得精确。

normal.en: Relativity does not mean that anything goes.
normal.cn: 相对论并不意味着什么都行。

abstract.en: Relativity is not the absence of truth but the presence of a frame.
abstract.cn: 相对性不是真理的缺席，而是参考系的存在。

abstract.en: To know your frame is the beginning of measuring anything.
abstract.cn: 知道自己的参考系，是测量任何事物的开端。

abstract.en: Even time bends when the frame is taken seriously.
abstract.cn: 当参考系被认真对待，连时间也会弯。

examples.en: Einstein's theory of relativity changed how we think about time.
examples.cn: 爱因斯坦的相对论改变了我们对时间的看法。

examples.en: The relativity of taste makes arguments about food endless.
examples.cn: 口味的相对性让关于食物的争论没有尽头。

examples.en: Special relativity explains why clocks on fast planes run slightly slow.
examples.cn: 狭义相对论解释了为什么高速飞机上的钟走得稍慢。

dict_mnemonic.text: relative（相对的）加 ity（名词尾）：一切都得相对于某物才成立，这种状态是相对性；把它写成物理定律，就是相对论。

root: 拉丁 relatus（被带回的）→ relativus（有关的）→ 英语 relative ＋ -ity → relativity；同族有 relative、relatively、relativist。

sensesIntro.en: The core is dependence on a frame; the senses move from a general condition of comparison to the physical theory of space and time.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「依赖参考系」；义项从一般的比较状态，到关于时空的物理理论。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two trains passing, each passenger sure that the other is moving.
core.cn: 核心意象：两列火车交错而过，月台上的人与车上的人各看到不同的运动。

branches.en: a taste that no one can rank
branches.cn: 无人能排序的口味

branches.en: clocks that disagree at speed
branches.cn: 高速下走得不一样的钟

branches.en: a common habit of comparison made exact
branches.cn: 被精确化的日常比较习惯

branches.en: gravity described as curved space
branches.cn: 用弯曲空间描述的引力

branches.en: a custom judged inside its own setting
branches.cn: 在自身环境中评判的习俗

intro.en: The adjective of comparison takes the Latin noun ending of quality, and the noun becomes the name of a physical theory.
intro.cn: 表比较的形容词接上拉丁表性质的名词词尾，这个名词随后成为一个物理理论的名称。

latinIntro.en: The stem is relativus, having relation to; -itas forms the noun of quality.
latinIntro.cn: 词干是 relativus（与其他事物有关的）；-itas 构成表性质的名词。

definition_zh: 打哈欠；哈欠；裂开；令人厌倦的事物
definition_en: to open the mouth wide and breathe in slowly when tired or bored, or the act of doing so
core_image: 开会到一半，有人仰起头，张大嘴，眼睛一起闭上
scene: 会议室里暖气太足，坐在后排的人一个接一个把嘴张得很大又合上。 She tried to hide the fact that she was yawning during the lecture.
sceneCN: 这里 yawn 是「打哈欠」（第 1 个义项：疲倦或无聊时张大嘴慢慢吸气）；句意为她努力掩饰自己在听讲座时打哈欠。会议室后排那张得很大的嘴，就是这个词的印象。

derivatives.zh: 由 yawn 加 -ing 构成，义为「打哈欠的；裂得很开的」
由 yawn 加 -er 构成，义为「打哈欠的人；乏味的东西」

senses.title: To open the mouth in tiredness
senses.definition: to open the mouth wide and breathe in deeply, usually because one is tired or bored
senses.definitionCN: 因疲倦或无聊而张大嘴深吸一口气
senses.example: She tried to hide the fact that she was yawning during the lecture.
senses.exampleCN: 她努力掩饰自己在听讲座时打哈欠。
senses.why: The oldest verb meant to open the mouth wide, and tiredness is simply the most common reason for doing it.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词最早的意思就是张大嘴，而疲倦只是做这个动作最常见的原因。

senses.title: The open mouth itself
senses.definition: the act or sound of opening the mouth wide and breathing in, taken as a sign of tiredness
senses.definitionCN: 张大嘴吸气这一动作，常被视为疲倦的表现
senses.example: He gave a long yawn before answering the question.
senses.exampleCN: 回答问题前他打了一个长长的哈欠。
senses.why: Any verb of a bodily action can be turned into a noun for that action, so the open mouth becomes a countable thing.
senses.whyCN: 任何表示身体动作的动词都能转成这个动作的名词，于是张嘴这件事变成了可数之物。

senses.title: The ground that opens wide
senses.definition: to open very wide, said of a hole, gap, or space
senses.definitionCN: 指洞口、裂缝或空间张得很大
senses.example: A yawning hole had opened in the road after the flood.
senses.exampleCN: 洪水过后，路面上裂开了一个大洞。
senses.why: Because the mouth opens wide when one yawns, the same word is used for any gap that opens just as wide.
senses.whyCN: 打哈欠时嘴张得很开，因此任何同样张得很大的裂口都用这个词。

senses.title: The boring thing
senses.definition: something so dull that it makes people yawn, used in informal speech
senses.definitionCN: 乏味得让人打哈欠的东西，多用于口语
senses.example: The second half of the film was a real yawn.
senses.exampleCN: 这部电影的后半段实在无聊。
senses.why: Since yawning signals boredom, the name of the action slides onto the boring thing that causes it.
senses.whyCN: 既然打哈欠表示无聊，这个动作的名字就滑到了引起它的无聊东西身上。

senses.title: The open mouth of an object
senses.definition: a wide opening, as of a cave or a valley, described by the same picture of a gaping mouth
senses.definitionCN: 洞穴或山谷等张开的宽大开口，用同一个「张嘴」的画面来形容
senses.example: The path led into the yawn of the cave.
senses.exampleCN: 小路通进那个张着大口的洞穴。
senses.why: The body picture is projected onto landscape, so a cave mouth is described with the same widening.
senses.whyCN: 身体的画面被投射到景物上，于是洞口也用同一种「张大」来描写。

intro.en: Yawn comes from an Old English verb for opening the mouth wide, and the family is shared with Dutch and German words of similar shape.
intro.cn: yawn 出自古英语中「张大嘴」的动词，与荷兰语、德语中形似的词同属一族。

items.en: A reconstructed Germanic verb described the mouth opening, with a long vowel at its centre.
items.cn: 重构的日耳曼语动词描写张嘴的动作，中间是一个长元音。

items.en: geonian meant to open the mouth wide, and was already used of the tired gesture.
items.cn: 古英语 geonian 意为张大嘴，当时已用于这个疲倦的动作。

items.en: The form shifted toward yane and yonen, and the spelling with w appeared later.
items.cn: 中古英语时期形式变为 yane、yonen，带 w 的拼写后来才出现。

items.en: The spelling settled as yawn, and the noun use followed the verb.
items.cn: 拼写固定为 yawn，名词用法随后从动词衍生出来。

items.en: The picture of a gaping mouth was extended to holes, gaps, and dull things.
items.cn: 张嘴的画面被扩用到洞口、裂缝和乏味的事物上。

note.en: Yawn is easily confused with look-alike words, and sits near a small group of tiredness words.
note.cn: yawn 容易与形近词混淆，也与一小群表示疲倦的词相邻。

entries.definition: a person who yawns, or something very boring
entries.definitionCN: 同根派生词，打哈欠的人，也指极无聊的事物

entries.definition: open very wide, as a gap
entries.definitionCN: 同根形式，张得很大的（如裂口）

entries.definition: an area of short cut grass, spelt almost the same but unrelated in origin
entries.definitionCN: 只是拼写相近，草坪，词源不同

entries.definition: to extend the arms and body when tired
entries.definitionCN: 相关动作，疲倦时伸展身体

entries.definition: to sleep lightly for a short time
to make someone feel tired and uninterested

normalIntro.en: Yawn is built on the picture of a mouth opening wide, and its relatives all keep that opening.
normalIntro.cn: yawn 建立在张嘴的画面之上，它的同族词也都保留着那个开口。

normal.en: The yawning gap in the road keeps the wide-open mouth of the original gesture.
normal.cn: 路上那个 yawning gap 保留了最初张嘴的宽大开口。

normal.en: Yawner is the person who yawns, and by extension anything so dull it makes you yawn.
normal.cn: yawner 指打哈欠的人，引申为任何无聊到让人打哈欠的东西。

normal.en: Old English geonian already meant to open the mouth, so the tired gesture is the oldest use.
normal.cn: 古英语 geonian 已经是「张嘴」，所以这个疲倦的动作是最早的用法。

normal.en: The noun and the verb share one spelling, so a yawn is both the act and the thing.
normal.cn: 名词与动词拼写相同，所以 yawn 既是动作也是那件事。

normal.en: Yawning is catching: seeing someone yawn often makes you yawn too, which keeps the word in daily talk.
normal.cn: 打哈欠会传染：看到别人打哈欠，自己也常跟着打，这个词因此常在日常话里出现。

abstract.en: Picture a meeting room where one mouth after another opens and closes like small doors.
abstract.cn: 想象一间会议室，一张张嘴像小门一样一个接一个打开又关上。

abstract.en: Picture a cave whose entrance is so wide it looks like a mouth mid-yawn.
abstract.cn: 想象一处洞口宽得像正张着嘴打哈欠。

abstract.en: Picture a dull film where the audience slowly sinks and the screen seems to widen into a black mouth.
abstract.cn: 想象一部无聊电影，观众慢慢往下沉，银幕仿佛张成一张黑洞洞的大嘴。

examples.en: She tried to hide the fact that she was yawning during the lecture.
examples.cn: 她努力掩饰自己在听讲座时打哈欠。

examples.en: He gave a long yawn before answering the question.
examples.cn: 回答问题前他打了一个长长的哈欠。

examples.en: A yawning hole had opened in the road after the flood.
examples.cn: 洪水过后，路面上裂开了一个大洞。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哟，嗯」——困得不行时有人仰头张嘴，喉咙里飘出一声「哟，嗯」，这个懒懒的开口动作就是 yawn。

root: 古英语 geonian（张大嘴），属日耳曼语族；与荷兰语 geeuwen、德语 gähnen 同源，词根只表示「张开」。

sensesIntro.en: Starting from a mouth opened wide, the word extends to the gaping openings of the world and to anything boring enough to cause it.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一张张大的嘴出发，这个词伸向世上各种张开的裂口，也伸向一切无聊到能引起它的东西。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a mouth opening very wide in tiredness
core.cn: 核心意象：疲倦时张得很大的一张嘴

branches.en: The tired gesture is the oldest and most common sense.
branches.cn: 疲倦时的这个动作是最古老也最常见的义项。

branches.en: The same act becomes a countable noun in daily speech.
branches.cn: 同一个动作在日常话里变成可数的名词。

branches.en: The wide opening is projected onto holes, caves, and valleys.
branches.cn: 张开的形状被投射到洞口、洞穴与山谷上。

branches.en: Boredom is the feeling that causes the gesture, and so names the dull thing.
branches.cn: 无聊是引起这个动作的感受，于是也用它的名字来称乏味之物。

branches.en: One widening movement ties the body and the landscape together.
branches.cn: 同一个张开动作把身体与景物连在了一起。

intro.en: Yawn is a native Germanic word that works as both verb and noun and forms a few adjectives in -ing.
intro.cn: yawn 是本土日耳曼语词，兼作动词和名词，并能加 -ing 构成形容词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin ancestor for this word, so the related forms below are its English family, not Latin roots.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁语来源，下面的相关形式是它的英语词族，而不是拉丁词根。

items.meaning: to open the mouth wide when tired
items.example: He yawned twice during the film.
items.exampleCN: 他看电影时打了两次哈欠。

items.meaning: both the act and the thing
items.example: A yawn escaped her before she could stop it.
items.exampleCN: 她还没来得及忍住，就打了个哈欠。

items.meaning: forming the adjective for a wide opening
items.meaningCN: 构成表示张得很开的形容词
items.example: A yawning gap separated the two sides.
items.exampleCN: 双方之间有一条巨大的鸿沟。

items.meaning: one who yawns, or a dull thing
items.meaningCN: 打哈欠的人，或乏味的东西
items.example: The speech was a real yawner.
items.exampleCN: 这场演讲真是让人打哈欠。

items.example: The yawning gap in pay worried the workers.
items.exampleCN: 薪酬上的巨大差距让工人们担忧。

items.meaning: to stop a yawn from showing
items.example: She stifled a yawn and kept listening.
items.exampleCN: 她忍住哈欠，继续听下去。

items.meaning: used of behaviour easily copied by others
items.meaningCN: 形容容易被别人跟着做的行为
items.example: Yawning is catching, especially in a warm room.
items.exampleCN: 打哈欠会传染，尤其在暖和的房间里。

items.meaning: to open the mouth wide or stare with it open
items.meaningCN: 相关的动词，张大嘴或张口瞪视
items.example: The crowd gaped at the huge screen.
items.exampleCN: 人群张着嘴盯着巨大的屏幕。

definition_zh: 没有价值的；无用的；不值钱的；毫无意义的
definition_en: having no value, use or importance
core_image: 一张被水泡烂的纸币摊在桌上，数字还在，却没人肯收
scene: 旧箱子里翻出一堆受潮的邮票，颜色都糊在一起了。 The painting turned out to be worthless, a copy made last year.
sceneCN: 这里 worthless 是「不值钱的」（第 1 个义项：没有市场价值）；句意为这幅画原来不值钱，是去年做的仿品。被水泡烂的钞票，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 形容词：没有价值的、无用的；不值钱的；毫无意义的

derivatives.zh: 名词，义为「价值」，是 worthless 的词干
名词，义为「无价值、无用」
形容词，义为「值得的、可敬的」，加 -y 构成的反向词
形容词，义为「值得做的」，由 worth 与 while 合成

senses.title: Having no money value
senses.definition: having no financial value, or almost none
senses.definitionCN: 没有或几乎没有金钱价值
senses.example: The painting turned out to be worthless, a copy made last year.
senses.exampleCN: 这幅画原来不值钱，是去年做的仿品。
senses.why: The -less ending simply removes worth; nothing is added in its place, so the gap is complete.
senses.whyCN: -less 尾缀只是把 worth 拿掉，什么也不补上，于是缺口彻底空了。

senses.title: Having no use
senses.titleCN: 无用：拿在手里也不解决问题
senses.definition: of no practical use for its purpose
senses.definitionCN: 对它的用途没有实际帮助
senses.example: The map was worthless after the old roads were closed.
senses.exampleCN: 老路封闭之后，那张地图就没用了。
senses.why: Here the value is usefulness: something that cannot do its job has lost the worth we hoped for.
senses.whyCN: 这里衡量的是用处：干不了自己该干的事，就失去我们寄望的价值。

senses.title: Of no importance
senses.definition: too slight to matter
senses.definitionCN: 太轻微而不值得在意
senses.example: Without the data, the argument is worthless.
senses.exampleCN: 没有数据支撑，这个论点毫无意义。
senses.why: Worth also means importance, and losing it leaves a claim that convinces nobody.
senses.whyCN: worth 也有重要性之义，一旦失去，论点就说服不了任何人。

senses.title: About a person
senses.titleCN: 一无是处：人觉得对自己没信心（口语）
senses.definition: used of a person who feels or is said to be of no account
senses.definitionCN: 指一个人觉得自己或被人说成一无是处
senses.example: Nobody is worthless, however badly they have failed.
senses.exampleCN: 不管失败得多惨，没有人是一无是处的。
senses.why: The word is harsh when used of people, because it judges the whole person, not one act.
senses.whyCN: 用来说人时很重，因为它评判的是整个人，而不是一件事。

intro.en: Worthless is the old English noun worth, value, plus the privative suffix -less.
intro.cn: worthless 是古英语名词 worth「价值」加上表缺失的后缀 -less。

items.en: The noun weorth meant value or price, the worth a thing carried.
items.cn: 名词 weorth 意为价值或价钱，即一物所承载的份量。

items.en: The adjective worthleas formed early, describing what had no price.
items.cn: 形容词 worthleas 形成很早，描述没有价钱的东西。

items.en: Germanic languages regularly formed a lacking word with -less, as German -los shows.
items.cn: 日耳曼诸语惯用 -less 这类尾缀造「缺失」之词，德语 -los 亦然。

items.en: Middle English kept the word and spread it from price to usefulness and importance.
items.cn: 中古英语保留了这个词，并把它从价钱扩展到用处与重要性。

items.en: Modern usage adds the moral and personal sense, so a person can be called worthless.
items.cn: 现代用法增添了道德与个人含义，于是人也可以被称为 worthless。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the worth- family; the near-meaning group holds adjectives of having little value.
note.cn: 形近组沿 worth- 家族；近义组收表示价值低微的形容词。

entries.definition: The noun and preposition behind the word: value, or deserving of.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或介词，义为「价值、值得」，本词的词干。

entries.definition: Deserving respect or effort; the opposite ending.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「值得的、可敬的」，尾缀正相反。

entries.definition: Worth the time spent, built from worth plus while.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「值得做的」，由 worth 与 while 合成。

entries.definition: The state of being without value.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「无价值」，加 -ness 构成。

entries.definition: Cannot do its job; close but about function.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「无用的」，侧重功能。

entries.definition: Without value, almost a synonym in price.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「无价值的」，在价钱上几乎同义。

entries.definition: Having no purpose, said of actions mainly.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「无意义的」，多用于行为。

entries.definition: Of great value; the opposite pole of the same scale.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「珍贵的」，同一尺度的另一端。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the privative -less and the many kinds of worth that can be lost.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子使用表缺失的 -less，以及可以被丢掉的多种价值。

normal.en: Worth is value, -less takes it away: worth + less = worthless.
normal.cn: worth 是价值，-less 拿掉它：worth 加 less 即成 worthless。

normal.en: A worthless note will not buy bread, no matter what the number says.
normal.cn: 不管票面写多少，废钞买不了面包。

normal.en: Worthless without data means the argument cannot stand alone.
normal.cn: 后接 without data，指论点无法独立成立。

normal.en: Worthless and priceless look alike but are opposites in price.
normal.cn: worthless 与 priceless 长得像，在价钱上却相反。

normal.en: Calling a person worthless attacks the person, not the work.
normal.cn: 说一个人 worthless，攻击的是人，不是做事。

abstract.en: The word is a subtraction, not an insult: worth has been removed and nothing put in its place.
abstract.cn: 这个词是做减法而不是骂人：价值被抽走，空位没有填。

abstract.en: Value is always value for someone, so worthless describes a relation, not a fact inside the thing.
abstract.cn: 价值总是对某人的价值，所以 worthless 描述的是一种关系，而非物内的事实。

abstract.en: Money, maps and promises all become worthless when the world they assumed disappears.
abstract.cn: 当世界变了样，钞票、地图与承诺都会变得毫无价值。

examples.en: The shares are now almost worthless.
examples.cn: 这些股票现在几乎一文不值。

examples.en: A promise made in anger is often worthless.
examples.cn: 气头上许下的承诺往往是空话。

examples.en: He felt worthless after losing the job.
examples.cn: 失业之后他觉得自己一无是处。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「沃思勒斯」——沃思（我思）勒斯（了死）也没想出价值：无价值的

root: 古英语名词 weorth「价值」加表缺失的后缀 -less，古英语已作 worthleas；同族词有 worth、worthy、worthwhile。

sensesIntro.en: Worthless measures price, usefulness, importance and, most harshly, a person’s sense of self.
sensesIntro.cn: worthless 衡量价钱、用处、重要性，最重的一层是对人的自我评价。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a soaked banknote, the number intact, no shop willing to take it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张泡烂的钞票，数字还在，却没人肯收。

branches.en: MONEY LINE: the market will not pay.
branches.cn: 金钱线：市场不肯付钱。

branches.en: TOOL LINE: it cannot do its job.
branches.cn: 工具线：它干不成自己的事。

branches.en: ARGUMENT LINE: nothing here convinces anyone.
branches.cn: 论证线：这里任何结论都说服不了人。

branches.en: PERSON LINE: a verdict on a whole life.
branches.cn: 人身线：对整个人生的判决。

branches.en: CONTRAST: valueless is about price, useless about function.
branches.cn: 对照线：valueless 谈价钱，useless 谈功能。

intro.en: Worthless is a stem plus a privative suffix; its family shows the same stem with other endings.
intro.cn: worthless 是词干加表缺失的后缀，家族里同一词干还接其他词尾。

latinIntro.en: Nothing Latin here: the word is native English, and -less descends from an old Germanic privative.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁成分：词是英语本土的，-less 源自日耳曼语的表缺失成分。

items.example: It forms worthwhile in older spellings.
items.exampleCN: 它在旧拼法里参与 worthwhile。

items.example: It is the opposite of worthless.
It shows the stem as a preposition.
items.exampleCN: 它展示词干作介词的用法。

definition_zh: 适用的；可应用的；相关的
definition_en: able to be applied to a situation, or relevant to a particular case
core_image: 一块正好扣上卡口的盖板
scene: 律师翻到条款最后一页，确认它是否适用于这起纠纷。 The rule is applicable to all members.
sceneCN: 这里 applicable 是「适用的」（第 1 个义项：能套用到某种情形上）；句意是这条规则适用于所有成员。

pos.zh: 形容词：适用的；可应用的

derivatives.zh: 动词：应用；申请
名词：应用；申请
名词：适用性

senses.title: Able to be applied
senses.definition: able to be used in a particular situation or to a particular person
senses.definitionCN: 能够用于特定情形或特定对象
senses.example: The rule is applicable to all members.
senses.exampleCN: 这条规则适用于所有成员。
senses.why: Applicable is apply plus -able, literally 'able to be applied', so it asks whether a rule or method fits the case.
senses.whyCN: applicable 是 apply 加 -able，字面即「可以被应用的」，因此它问的是规则或方法是否对得上这个情形。

senses.title: Relevant to the matter
senses.definition: directly connected with the subject being discussed
senses.definitionCN: 与正在讨论的主题直接相关
senses.example: Please attach any applicable documents.
senses.exampleCN: 请附上任何相关文件。
senses.why: If something can be applied to the case, it belongs to the case, which is how the word also comes to mean relevant.
senses.whyCN: 如果某物能套用到这个案子上，它就属于这个案子，于是这个词也有了「相关」的意思。

intro.en: Applicable is the adjective of apply, meaning 'able to be put to use'.
intro.cn: applicable 是 apply 的形容词，意为「可以被投入使用的」。

items.en: plicare meant 'to fold'.
items.cn: plicare 意为「折叠」。

items.en: applicare meant 'to fold to, attach'.
items.cn: applicare 意为「贴上去、附着」。

items.en: English apply developed the sense 'to put to use'.
items.cn: 英语 apply 发展出「应用」的含义。

items.en: Applicable was formed with the suffix -able.
items.cn: applicable 由词尾 -able 构成。

items.en: The word is now standard in legal and technical writing.
items.cn: 现代这个词在法律与技术写作中很常见。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the apply root; the near-meaning group gives other words of relevance.
note.cn: 形近组共享 apply 词根；近义组是其他表示相关性的词。

entries.definition: to put to use
one who applies
a device
connected with the matter
right for the purpose
directly relevant

normalIntro.en: Applicable asks: can this rule be laid onto this case?
normalIntro.cn: applicable 问的是：这条规则能扣到这个案子上吗？

normal.en: Applicable to is the standard preposition pair.
normal.cn: applicable to 是标准介词搭配。

normal.en: Where applicable appears often in forms and contracts.
normal.cn: where applicable 常见于表格与合同。

normal.en: The noun applicability is more formal than applicable.
normal.cn: 名词 applicability 比 applicable 更正式。

normal.en: The American stress falls on the first syllable: AP-pli-ca-ble.
normal.cn: 美式重音落在第一个音节：AP-pli-ca-ble。

normal.en: Do not confuse applicable with applied; one is a fit, the other is an action.
normal.cn: 不要混淆 applicable 与 applied，一个表示契合，一个表示动作。

abstract.en: See a cover snapping into a matching slot.
abstract.cn: 想象盖板正好扣进卡槽。

abstract.en: See a stamp pressed onto the right form.
abstract.cn: 想象印章盖在正确的表格上。

abstract.en: See a key that turns only in one lock.
abstract.cn: 想象只在一把锁里转得动的钥匙。

examples.en: The rule is applicable to all members.
examples.cn: 这条规则适用于所有成员。

examples.en: Please attach any applicable documents.
examples.cn: 请附上任何相关文件。

examples.en: The discount is applicable only in June.
examples.cn: 这项折扣只在六月适用。

dict_mnemonic.text: apply（应用）加 -able（可……的）：可以应用的，适用的。

root: 由动词 apply 加形容词词尾 -able 构成；apply 源于拉丁语 applicare「贴上、附着」，故本义为「可以被贴上去的」。

sensesIntro.en: Being able to be applied and being relevant to the case are two sides of one fit.
sensesIntro.cn: 「能被应用」与「与本案相关」是同一契合关系的两面。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a part that fits exactly into its slot.
core.cn: 核心意象：恰好嵌入卡槽的部件。

branches.en: applicable to all
branches.cn: 适用于所有人

branches.en: applicable law
branches.cn: 适用法律

branches.en: universally applicable
branches.cn: 普遍适用

branches.en: where applicable
branches.cn: 在适用情况下

branches.en: applicable documents
branches.cn: 相关文件

intro.en: An -able adjective on the apply root, common in rules and contracts.
intro.cn: 这是一个建立在 apply 词根上的 -able 形容词，常见于规则与合同。

latinIntro.en: The root plicare, 'to fold', also gives complicate and explicit.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 plicare「折叠」也派生出 complicate 与 explicit。

definition_zh: 积累；积聚；堆积
definition_en: to collect or increase in quantity gradually over a period of time
core_image: 雪球顺着斜坡滚下，一路把新雪粘到身上
scene: 老屋已经很久没人住了，琴盖上落了厚厚一层灰。 Dust had accumulated on the old piano.
sceneCN: 这里的 accumulate 是「堆积」（第 2 个义项：东西一点点堆在一处）；句意是旧钢琴上积了一层灰。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加名词后缀构成，义为「积累；堆积物」
由词干加形容词后缀构成，义为「累积的」
由词干加表示施动者的后缀构成，义为「蓄能器；累加器」

senses.title: To build up something valuable
senses.definition: to gather more and more of something useful or valuable over time
senses.definitionCN: 随着时间推移，把有用的或有价值的东西越聚越多
senses.example: She accumulated a large collection of rare books.
senses.exampleCN: 她积累了一大批珍本书。
senses.why: The Latin noun cumulus names a heap, and ad- points things towards it, so the verb pictures valuables being heaped into one store.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁名词 cumulus 指「堆」，前缀 ad- 表示「朝着一处」，所以这个词画出的是把有价值的东西往同一个仓里堆。

senses.title: To pile up in one place
senses.definition: to collect in a growing pile, usually without anyone arranging it
senses.definitionCN: 东西无人整理地越堆越多，聚在一处
senses.example: Snow accumulated against the garden wall.
senses.exampleCN: 雪在院墙边越积越高。
senses.why: The same heap image turns literal: snow, dust and papers have no owner adding them, yet they still form a cumulus.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「堆」的意象在这里变成实景：雪、灰和纸张并没有人刻意去添，却照样堆成一个土丘似的形状。

senses.title: To grow in intensity
senses.definition: to increase gradually until a feeling or problem becomes strong
senses.definitionCN: 情绪或问题逐渐加重，直到变得强烈
senses.example: Tension accumulated between the two neighbours.
senses.exampleCN: 两个邻居之间的紧张情绪越积越重。
senses.why: A heap can be made of feelings as well as objects; each small grievance adds one more layer until the mass presses down.
senses.whyCN: 堆起来的不只是实物，也可以是情绪；每一次小小的不满都加一层，最后整堆重量压了下来。

intro.en: The word is Latin in both parts: a prefix of direction and a noun for a heap.
intro.cn: 这个词的两半都来自拉丁语：一个表示方向的前缀，一个表示「堆」的名词。

items.en: cumulus meant a heap, a mass or a pile.

items.en: accumulare joined ad-, towards, with cumulus, to heap something up.
items.cn: accumulare 把表示「朝向」的 ad- 与 cumulus 结合，意为把东西堆起来。

items.en: the participle accumulatus described what had been piled together.
items.cn: 分词 accumulatus 描述已经堆在一起的东西。

items.en: accumulate entered English as a learned verb of heaping and adding.
items.cn: accumulate 在十五世纪进入英语，是书面语中表示「堆叠、添加」的动词。

items.en: it now covers money, data, experience, dust and even stress.

a device that stores energy or numbers
increasing by successive additions
