definition_zh: 多元主义；多元性；多重性；多元论
definition_en: the belief that different groups, cultures or opinions can and should coexist; the state of existing in more than one form or centre; and the philosophical view that reality contains many independent things
core_image: 一张长桌边坐着服饰各异的人，桌上摆着颜色不同的菜
scene: 社区中心的厨房里，几家人各自端来一盘家乡菜，摆在同一张长桌上。 The festival was built on a simple pluralism: every community brought its own dish and its own music.
sceneCN: 这里 pluralism 是「多元主义」（第 1 个义项：不同群体与文化并存并受尊重的主张）；句意为这个节日建立在一种朴素的多元主义之上：每个社群带来自己的食物与音乐。图中可辨识物件：长桌、各家的菜盘、乐器。

pos.zh: 多元主义；多元性；多重性

derivatives.zh: 由 plural 加表示「主张者」的后缀 -ist 构成，义为「多元主义者」
由 pluralist 加 -ic 构成，义为「多元主义的；多元的」
与 pluralism 同出拉丁词根 plur-，义为「多数；多样性」

senses.title: The view that different groups should coexist
senses.definition: the belief or policy that different ethnic, cultural or religious groups can and should live together without any of them being forced to disappear
senses.definitionCN: 认为不同族群、文化或宗教群体能够并且应当共存、任何一方都不应被强迫消失的信念或政策
senses.example: The festival was built on a simple pluralism: every community brought its own dish and its own music.
senses.exampleCN: 这个节日建立在一种朴素的多元主义之上：每个社群带来自己的食物与音乐。
senses.why: The suffix -ism turns plural into the name of a position, so pluralism is not merely the fact of being many but the deliberate view that being many is good and must be protected.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ism 把 plural 变成一个立场的名称，所以 pluralism 不只是「有很多」这个事实，而是有意主张「多」是好事、必须受到保护的观点。

senses.title: The state of being multiple
senses.definition: the condition of existing in more than one form, source or centre rather than in a single one
senses.definitionCN: 以不止一种形式、来源或中心存在，而不是只有单一形式、来源或中心的状态
senses.example: The report describes a pluralism of legal systems in the border region.
senses.exampleCN: 报告描述了边境地区法律体系的多重并存。
senses.why: Because -ism can also name a condition rather than a doctrine, pluralism is used for any arrangement with several centres: several legal systems, several sources of authority, several centres of power.
senses.whyCN: 因为 -ism 也能指一种状态而非一套学说，pluralism 便用来指任何有多个中心的安排：多套法律体系、多个权威来源、多个权力中心。

senses.title: The philosophical view that reality has many parts
senses.definition: the philosophical position that reality consists of many independent substances or principles rather than a single one
senses.definitionCN: 认为实在由许多独立实体或原理构成、而非由单一本原构成的哲学立场
senses.example: William James defended a pluralism in which no single system could contain the whole world.
senses.exampleCN: 威廉·詹姆斯主张一种多元论：没有任何单一体系能容纳整个世界。
senses.why: Philosophy took the word from the plain count of many things and made it the opposite of monism: if monism says reality is one, pluralism says its parts are genuinely many and cannot be reduced to one.
senses.whyCN: 哲学从「多」这个平常的计数出发，把它变成一元论的对立面：如果说一元论主张实在是一，多元论就主张它的各部分确实为多，无法化归为一。

intro.en: Pluralism is a modern coinage that joins Latin pluralis, of more than one, with the suffix -ism, which came from Greek through Latin and names a doctrine, a practice or a condition.
intro.cn: pluralism 是近代新造的词，把拉丁语 pluralis（属于不止一个的）与后缀 -ism 结合起来；后者经拉丁语来自希腊语，用来指一种学说、实践或状态。

items.en: Pluralis, from plus, more, meant belonging to more than one and named the grammatical plural.
items.cn: pluralis 源自 plus（更多），意为「属于不止一个的」，并指语法上的复数。

items.en: The suffix came from Greek -ismos through Latin -ismus, and named a practice, a doctrine or a condition.
items.cn: 这个后缀经拉丁语 -ismus 来自希腊语 -ismos，用来指一种实践、学说或状态。

items.en: English -ism attaches to nouns to name a system of belief, as in realism or socialism, and was ready to do the same with plural.
items.cn: 英语的 -ism 附着在名词后指一套信念体系，如 realism 或 socialism，也随时可以与 plural 结合。

items.en: Pluralism appears in nineteenth-century English for philosophical and religious positions that accept many ultimate things or many valid traditions.
items.cn: pluralism 在十九世纪英语中出现，用于接受多种终极存在或多种有效传统的哲学与宗教立场。

items.en: Modern English applies it to societies, legal systems and politics, where many groups or centres share one space.
items.cn: 现代英语把它用于社会、法律体系与政治，指许多群体或中心共享同一空间。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the words built on the plural stem and its suffixes; the near-meaning group gathers words for diversity and coexistence, plus the position it opposes.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在 plural 词干及其后缀上的词；近义组收表示多样与共存的词，以及它所反对的立场。

entries.definition: A person who holds or supports pluralism.
entries.definitionCN: 持有或支持多元主义的人。

entries.definition: Organized around several groups or principles rather than one.
entries.definitionCN: 围绕多个群体或原理而非单一者组织的。

entries.definition: The state of being many, or the largest vote short of a majority.
entries.definitionCN: 多数的状态，或未过半但最多的票数。

entries.definition: The grammatical form for more than one; the stem that this word extends.
entries.definitionCN: 表示不止一个的语法形式；这个词所扩展的词干。

entries.definition: The presence of many different kinds within one group or place.
entries.definitionCN: 同一群体或地点内存在许多不同种类。

entries.definition: A policy that values several cultures living side by side.
entries.definitionCN: 重视多种文化并存的立场或政策。

entries.definition: Willingness to accept views or groups one disagrees with.
entries.definitionCN: 愿意接受自己不同意的观点或群体。

entries.definition: The view that reality comes from a single substance or principle.
entries.definitionCN: 认为实在出自单一实体或原理的立场；一元论。

normalIntro.en: The word joins the Latin stem for more to the suffix of doctrines, and the family keeps moving between a fact, a policy and a philosophy.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词把拉丁语表示「更多」的词干接在表示学说的后缀上，词族在事实、政策与哲学之间来回移动。

normal.en: Pluralis is the Latin adjective for belonging to more than one, and -ism names a doctrine, so pluralism is literally the doctrine of the many.
normal.cn: pluralis 是拉丁语中表示「属于不止一个」的形容词，-ism 指一种主张，所以 pluralism 字面上就是「多的学说」。

normal.en: The same word can name a fact, as in a pluralism of legal systems, and a value, as in cultural pluralism.
normal.cn: 同一个词既能指事实，如法律体系的多重并存，也能指价值，如文化多元主义。

normal.en: Pluralism and plural share the stem plur-, which also gives plurality and plus, all pointing at more than one.
normal.cn: pluralism 与 plural 共用词干 plur-，这个词干也生出 plurality 与 plus，都指向「不止一个」。

normal.en: Pluralist is the person, pluralistic is the adjective, and pluralism is the position or the condition.
normal.cn: pluralist 指人，pluralistic 是形容词，pluralism 指这种立场或状态。

normal.en: In philosophy pluralism is the opposite of monism, just as in grammar plural is the opposite of singular.
normal.cn: 哲学上 pluralism 是一元论的对立面，正如语法上复数与单数相对。

abstract.en: Pluralism is the wager that a table with many dishes feeds more people than a table with one.
abstract.cn: 多元主义是一场押注：摆着许多盘菜的桌子，比只摆一盘的桌子更能养活人。

abstract.en: A fact becomes a value the moment someone decides that many centres are worth keeping.
abstract.cn: 当有人认定多个中心值得保留时，事实就变成了价值。

abstract.en: The word asks a simple question: must one account of the world replace all the others?
abstract.cn: 这个词问一个简单的问题：关于世界的某一种说法，是否必须取代其余全部？

examples.en: The festival was built on a simple pluralism: every community brought its own dish and its own music.
examples.cn: 这个节日建立在一种朴素的多元主义之上：每个社群带来自己的食物与音乐。

examples.en: The report describes a pluralism of legal systems in the border region.
examples.cn: 报告描述了边境地区法律体系的多重并存。

examples.en: William James defended a pluralism in which no single system could contain the whole world.
examples.cn: 威廉·詹姆斯主张一种多元论：没有任何单一体系能容纳整个世界。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普露拉」——各家的露水落在同一片草地上，彼此并存；记住 pluralism 是多元主义。

root: 拉丁语 plus（更多）→ pluralis（属于不止一个的）→ 英语 plural；再加经拉丁语来自希腊语的后缀 -ism（学说、制度），构成 pluralism。词根 plur- 表示「多」，同族词还有 plurality、pluralist。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the value placed on many; the senses run from a social belief in coexistence, to the plain condition of having several centres, to the philosophical view that reality itself is many.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是对「多」的看重；义项从社会层面的共存主张，走到拥有多个中心的实际状态，再到认为实在本身就是多的哲学立场。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one long table where families in different clothes set down dishes of different colours.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张长桌边坐着服饰各异的人，桌上摆着颜色不同的菜。

branches.en: neighbours bringing different dishes to one table
branches.cn: 邻居把不同的菜端上同一张桌

branches.en: a street with a mosque, a church and a shrine
branches.cn: 一条街上并立的清真寺、教堂与神龛

branches.en: two legal systems sharing one border town
branches.cn: 两套法律体系共处一个边镇

branches.en: power split among several centres
branches.cn: 权力分散在几个中心

branches.en: a philosopher refusing one single system
branches.cn: 拒绝单一体系的哲学家

intro.en: The word is a Latin adjective of plurality with the Greek-derived suffix of doctrines, and English adds the usual endings for a holder and a quality.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语中表示多数的形容词接上源自希腊语的学说后缀，英语又加上表示持有者与性质的后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin forms stand behind the word: pluralis, of more than one, its source plus, more, and the noun pluralitas, a plurality.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词背后有可考的拉丁形式：pluralis（属于不止一个的）、它的来源 plus（更多），以及名词 pluralitas（多数）。

definition_zh: 宣言；声明；申报
definition_en: an official or formal statement
core_image: 广场上被大声念出的那张纸
scene: 代表们站在台阶上，把那份文件读给人群听。 The declaration was read aloud to the crowd.
sceneCN: 这里 declaration 指「宣言」（第 1 个义项：正式公开的声明）；句意是宣言被当众朗读。

derivatives.zh: 宣布
陈述的
宣告性的
声明者

senses.title: A public formal statement
senses.definition: a formal statement made openly and put on record
senses.definitionCN: 公开作出并被记录下来的正式声明
senses.example: The declaration was read aloud to the crowd.
senses.exampleCN: 宣言被当众朗读。
senses.why: Saying it in public makes the words hard to take back.
senses.whyCN: 当众说出口，这些话就收不回去了。

senses.title: A statement for customs
senses.definition: a written list of goods or income given to officials
senses.definitionCN: 交给官员的货物或收入清单
senses.example: Fill in the declaration before you reach the desk.
senses.exampleCN: 走到柜台之前先把申报单填好。
senses.why: The state needs a paper version of what you carry.
senses.whyCN: 国家需要你随身带的东西有一份纸质版本。

senses.title: The act of announcing
senses.definition: the act of announcing something officially
senses.definitionCN: 正式宣布某事的行为
senses.example: The declaration of the winner ended the match.
senses.exampleCN: 宣布获胜者终结了这场比赛。
senses.why: Naming an act and naming the paper use one word.
senses.whyCN: 指行为还是指那张纸，用的是同一个词。

intro.en: Declaration is Latin declaratio, from declarare, to make clear, built on clarus, bright.
intro.cn: declaration 即拉丁语 declaratio，来自 declarare（使清楚），根子是 clarus（明亮的）。

items.en: Clarus meant bright and easy to see.
items.cn: clarus 指明亮的、看得清的。

items.en: Declarare meant to make a matter clear to others.
items.cn: declarare 指把事情向别人说清楚。

items.en: Déclaration meant a public statement.
items.cn: déclaration 指公开的声明。

items.en: Declaration entered English as a formal announcement.
items.cn: declaration 作为正式公告进入英语。

items.en: Forms and customs gave it a plain official use.
items.cn: 表格与海关给了它一个朴素的官方用途。

note.en: The look-alike group all end in -ation, and the meaning group names public forms of saying.
note.cn: 形近组都以 -ation 收尾，近义组则列出各种公开说法。

entries.definition: a downward slope or a turning aside
a slowing down in speed
the recovery of land or waste material
something said or written clearly
entries.definitionCN: 清楚说出或写下的内容

entries.definition: a public notice of news
an official public declaration

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with words read from a step and end with a form filled in at an airport desk.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从台阶上念出的文字开始，落到机场柜台前填好的一张表。

normal.en: A declaration is a sentence said where everyone can hear it.
normal.cn: 宣言就是一句在人人听得见的地方说出的话。

normal.en: Paper makes a promise heavier.
normal.cn: 纸让承诺变沉。

normal.en: Declare it once in public and you own it for ever.
normal.cn: 当众讲一次，它就永远归你负责。

normal.en: Customs asks for a list, not a speech.
normal.cn: 海关要的是一张清单，不是一番演讲。

normal.en: Clarus meant bright; a declaration brings a fact into the light.
normal.cn: clarus 本指明亮，宣言就是把事实拿到光下。

abstract.en: Picture a page held up above a crowd.
abstract.cn: 想象一页纸被举在人群上方。

abstract.en: Picture a stamp coming down on a form.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚印章落在表格上。

abstract.en: Picture a name read out and a room going quiet.
abstract.cn: 想象一个名字被念出，全场安静下来。

examples.en: The declaration was read aloud to the crowd.
examples.cn: 宣言被当众朗读。

examples.en: You must sign the customs declaration at the airport.
examples.cn: 在机场你必须签一份海关申报单。

examples.en: Their declaration of friendship surprised the reporters.
examples.cn: 他们公开的友好声明让记者们感到意外。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 declaration 记成「得客来声明」：de 是得，claration 听着像「客来声」，客人一到，主人得公开说一句欢迎。

root: 来自拉丁语 declaratio，动词 declarare 意为「使清楚」，根子是 clarus（明亮的）。十五世纪进入英语时指正式的公开公告，后来也用来指海关申报这类书面说明，以及「宣告」这个动作本身。

sensesIntro.en: From words said aloud in public, to a list handed to officials, to the act behind both.
sensesIntro.cn: 从当众说出的文字，到交给官员的一张清单，再到两者背后的那个动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a page held up and read out above a crowd.
core.cn: 核心意象：一页纸在人群上方被举起并朗读。

branches.en: The first sense is the open speech that everyone hears.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是人人听得见的那段公开讲话。

branches.en: The second sense is the same openness pressed into a form.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是同样的公开，被压进一张表格里。

branches.en: The third sense is the act that produces either one.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是产生前两者的那个动作。

branches.en: A speech and a form both turn a private fact into a record.
branches.cn: 讲话和表格，都把私事变成了记录。

branches.en: What is declared in words can later be checked against paper.
branches.cn: 口头宣告的东西，日后能拿纸来核对。

intro.en: Declaration belongs to the clar- family: clear, clarify, declare, declarative.
intro.cn: declaration 属于 clar- 这一族：clear、clarify、declare、declarative。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root is clarus, bright or clear, with clarare meaning to make bright.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根是 clarus（明亮、清楚），clarare 意为使明亮。

items.example: They declared the results at nine.

items.meaning: having the nature of a declaration
items.example: The court issued a declaratory ruling.
items.exampleCN: 法院作出了一项宣告性裁定。

items.example: The declarer signed at the bottom.

items.exampleCN: 他们公开宣称的目标是和平。

items.example: Undeclared goods were found in the bag.
items.exampleCN: 包里发现了未申报的物品。

items.example: Keep the declaration form in your hand.

latinEntries.example: Clarus gives English clear, clarify and declare.
latinEntries.exampleCN: clarus 给英语带来 clear、clarify 和 declare。

definition_zh: 热情地；热心地
definition_en: in a way that shows strong excitement and interest
core_image: 挥着手、提高声音，把一件事说得像节日一样
scene: 孩子们一边鼓掌一边热情地喊出队名。 The children clapped and shouted the team name enthusiastically.
sceneCN: 这里 enthusiastically 是「热情地」（第 1 个义项：以充满热情的方式）；句意：孩子们一边鼓掌，一边热情地喊出队名。

derivatives.zh: 热情的
热情；热忱
热衷者；爱好者

senses.title: With strong excitement
senses.definition: in a way that shows great excitement and interest
senses.definitionCN: 以表现出强烈兴奋与兴趣的方式
senses.example: She talked enthusiastically about her new job.
senses.exampleCN: 她热情地谈起自己的新工作。
senses.why: The adverb describes how an action is done, adding the heat of enthusiasm to the verb.
senses.whyCN: 副词描述动作如何进行，把 enthusiasm 的热度加到动词上。

senses.title: With eager approval
senses.definition: in a way that shows strong and warm support
senses.definitionCN: 以表现出强烈而热烈支持的方式
senses.example: The committee enthusiastically approved the new design.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会热烈地通过了新设计。
senses.why: Approval performed with excitement becomes enthusiastic approval.
senses.whyCN: 带着兴奋去赞同，就成为「热烈赞同」。

senses.title: With energetic effort
senses.definition: with a lot of energy and willingness to work
senses.definitionCN: 带着充沛精力与工作意愿
senses.example: He worked enthusiastically on the garden all summer.
senses.exampleCN: 他整个夏天都干劲十足地打理花园。
senses.why: The same inner fire can power steady work, not only speech.
senses.whyCN: 同样的内心之火也能驱动持续的工作，而不只是说话。

intro.en: Enthusiastically is enthusiastic plus -ally, the adverb ending used after adjectives in -ic.
intro.cn: enthusiastically 是 enthusiastic 加 -ally，这是 -ic 结尾形容词常用的副词词尾。

items.en: Theos means god, and entheos means inspired.
items.cn: theos 意为神，entheos 意为受神启的。

items.en: Enthousiasmos means divine possession.
items.cn: enthousiasmos 意为神灵附体。

items.en: Enthusiasmus carries the noun into Latin.
items.cn: enthusiasmus 把这个名词带入拉丁语。

items.en: Enthusiasm and enthusiastic settle into English usage.
items.cn: enthusiasm 与 enthusiastic 进入英语用法。

items.en: The adverb enthusiastically appears with the -ally ending.
items.cn: 到 17 世纪，带 -ally 词尾的副词 enthusiastically 出现。

items.en: The adverb describes speech, support, and effort alike.
items.cn: 现代英语中，这个副词既可描述言语，也可描述支持与努力。

note.en: Enthusiastically is the adverb of enthusiastic, and it sits near eagerly and warmly.
note.cn: enthusiastically 是 enthusiastic 的副词，与 eagerly 和 warmly 相邻。

entries.definition: showing strong excitement
strong excited interest
a person who is very interested
in a way that shows strong desire
in a friendly and enthusiastic way
with strong interest or intensity

normalIntro.en: Enthusiastically is enthusiastic plus -ally, the standard adverb ending after -ic.
normalIntro.cn: enthusiastically 是 enthusiastic 加 -ally，这是 -ic 结尾形容词后的标准副词词尾。

normal.en: Adjectives ending in -ic usually take -ally, not just -ly.
normal.cn: -ic 结尾的形容词通常加 -ally，而不是只加 -ly。

normal.en: The adverb answers the question how: how did they respond? Enthusiastically.
normal.cn: 这个副词回答「怎样」：他们怎样回应？热情地。

normal.en: Speak enthusiastically is a common collocation.
normal.cn: speak enthusiastically 是常见搭配。

normal.en: The word often appears at the end of a sentence.
normal.cn: 这个词常出现在句末。

normal.en: Compare eagerly: eagerly stresses wanting, while enthusiastically stresses feeling.
normal.cn: 对比 eagerly：eagerly 强调「想要」，enthusiastically 强调「情感」。

abstract.en: Picture a crowd on its feet before the song ends.
abstract.cn: 想象歌还没唱完，观众已经全体起立。

abstract.en: Imagine a handshake that pulls the other person forward.
abstract.cn: 想象一次把对方拉近的握手。

abstract.en: Think of a voice rising at the end of a sentence.
abstract.cn: 想象句尾时声音扬起来。

examples.en: She talked enthusiastically about her new job.
examples.cn: 她热情地谈起自己的新工作。

examples.en: The committee enthusiastically approved the new design.
examples.cn: 委员会热烈地通过了新设计。

examples.en: He worked enthusiastically on the garden all summer.
examples.cn: 他整个夏天都干劲十足地打理花园。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「enthusiastic + ally」——热情像盟友一样跟着每个动作，就是热情地；这只是构词联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 theos（神）→ entheos（心中有神的）→ enthousiasmos（受神启的激情）→ enthusiasm → enthusiastic ＋ -ally → enthusiastically。

sensesIntro.en: The adverb carries the fire of enthusiasm into verbs, describing excited speech, warm approval, and energetic effort.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个副词把 enthusiasm 的火带进动词，描述兴奋的言语、热烈的赞同与充沛的努力。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a gesture and a raised voice carrying feeling into action.
core.cn: 核心意象：手势与提高的声音把感情带进动作。

branches.en: Excited speech is the most common use of the adverb.
branches.cn: 兴奋的言语，是这个副词最常见的用法。

branches.en: Warm approval makes agreement sound louder.
branches.cn: 热烈赞同让同意听起来更响亮。

branches.en: Energetic effort turns feeling into sustained work.
branches.cn: 充沛的努力把感情变成持续的工作。

branches.en: Speech and approval often share the same rising tone.
branches.cn: 言语与赞同常共享同一种上扬的语调。

branches.en: Approval can set a whole team to work with energy.
branches.cn: 赞同能让整个团队干劲十足地开工。

intro.en: Enthusiastically is the adverb of enthusiastic, built with the ending -ally.
intro.cn: enthusiastically 是 enthusiastic 的副词，由词尾 -ally 构成。

latinIntro.en: The chain runs from Greek theos, god, through enthusiasm, to the English adjective and its adverb.
latinIntro.cn: 这条链从希腊语 theos（神）经 enthusiasm，延伸到英语形容词及其副词。

items.example: Theos is the root of the family.
items.exampleCN: theos 是这个词族的根源。

items.example: Entheos gives the inner fire image.
items.exampleCN: entheos 提供内心之火的意象。

definition_zh: 拖拉机；牵引车
definition_en: a heavy vehicle with big rear wheels, used on farms to pull ploughs and trailers
core_image: 一台高大的拖拉机拖着犁，在田里翻出一道深沟
scene: 春天的地还硬着，一台高大的车拖着犁从田头开过去，留下整齐的沟。 The farmer drove the tractor across the field before the rain came.
sceneCN: 这里 tractor 是「拖拉机」（第 1 个义项：农田上用来牵引农具的重型车辆）；句意为农夫在雨来之前把拖拉机开过了田。

derivatives.zh: 由同一拉丁词干加 -tion 构成，义为「牵引；牵引力」
由词干加 -ive 构成，义为「牵引的」
与 tractor 同源，义为「一片土地；管道」

senses.title: The farm machine that pulls
senses.definition: a powerful farm vehicle with large wheels, used to pull ploughs and heavy loads
senses.definitionCN: 装有巨大车轮、用来拖犁和重物的农用动力车
senses.example: One tractor can plough the whole field in an afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 一台拖拉机一个下午就能把整块地犁完。
senses.why: The word is literally the puller, and on a farm the machine that pulls is this one.
senses.whyCN: 这个词字面意思就是「拉的车」，而在农场上负责拉的就是它。

senses.title: A vehicle for towing on the road
senses.definition: a short powerful motor vehicle used to haul a trailer or a broken-down lorry
senses.definitionCN: 用来拖挂车或拖走抛锚货车的短小动力车
senses.example: A tractor arrived to pull the lorry off the verge.
senses.exampleCN: 一辆牵引车开来把货车从路边拖走了。
senses.why: The same pulling job is done in towns and motorways, so the name follows the function off the farm.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「拉」的任务在城镇与公路上也在执行，于是这个名字跟着功能离开了农田。

senses.title: A blade worked by a motor
senses.definition: in the phrase lawn tractor, a riding mower that pulls itself over the grass
senses.definitionCN: lawn tractor 一类说法中，自行在草地上牵引前进的乘骑式割草机
senses.example: He cut the whole lawn with a small garden tractor.
senses.exampleCN: 他用一台小型园用牵引机割完了整片草坪。
senses.why: Any motor-driven tool that drags itself forward inherits the name because the pulling idea is still visible.
senses.whyCN: 任何靠马达拖着自己前进的工具都能继承这个名字，因为「拉」的意象仍然可见。

intro.en: Tractor is a coined Latin word, from trahere, to pull, with the agent ending -or, and it was applied to motor vehicles in the late nineteenth century.
intro.cn: tractor 是仿拉丁语构词法造的，由 trahere（拉）加施动后缀 -or 构成，十九世纪末被用来指机动车辆。

items.en: Trahere means to pull, draw, or drag, and its stem tract- underlies a large family in English.
items.cn: 拉丁语 trahere 意为拉、拖，其词干 tract- 在英语中撑起了一个大家族。

items.en: The Latin agent form tractor, meaning a puller, appears in English in the seventeenth century as a term of logic and medicine.
items.cn: 拉丁语施动形式 tractor 意为「拉的东西」，十七世纪在英语中作为逻辑学与医学术语出现。

items.en: In the 1890s the word is taken up for the new steam and petrol engines designed to pull ploughs.
items.cn: 十九世纪九十年代，这个词被用来指新出现的、专为拖犁设计的蒸汽与汽油发动机。

items.en: Twentieth-century mass farming makes the tractor a standard word, and the shortened slang tractor follows.
items.cn: 二十世纪的大规模农业让拖拉机成为常用词，其简称 tractor 也随之固定。

items.en: The idea widens again to road towing vehicles and to riding mowers in the later twentieth century.
items.cn: 二十世纪后期，这一概念再次扩展到公路牵引车与乘骑式割草机。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words with the same Latin pulling stem, and the near-meaning group gathers farm and hauling machines.
note.cn: 形近组收集同用拉丁语「拉」词干的词，近义组收集农用与拖运的机械。

entries.definition: the power of pulling, or grip on the ground
a large area of land
to pull towards
an imaginary pulling ray in science fiction
a farm tool that turns the soil
a machine that cuts and gathers crops
a heavy machine that pushes earth

normalIntro.en: These memories work from the Latin pulling stem, from the -or ending that marks the doer, and from the farm picture.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几条从拉丁语「拉」的词干、表示施动者的 -or 词尾以及农田画面入手。

normal.en: Trahere is to pull, and -or marks the one that pulls, so tractor is simply the puller.
normal.cn: trahere 是拉，-or 标记拉的那个，所以 tractor 就是「拉着的东西」。

normal.en: Tract, traction, tractor: land pulled together, grip pulled, and the machine that pulls.
normal.cn: tract、traction、tractor 分别是「拉成的土地」「拉的抓力」与「拉的车」。

normal.en: Attract, extract, contract: the same stem with a- for towards, ex- for out, con- for together.
normal.cn: attract、extract、contract 用同一词干，配 a- 表示朝向、ex- 表示向外、con- 表示一起。

normal.en: A tractor is recognised by big back wheels, because those wheels must grip while pulling.
normal.cn: 拖拉机的标志是后轮特别大，因为拖东西时轮子必须抓住地面。

normal.en: Traction is the property, tractor is the user of that property.
normal.cn: traction 是那种性质，tractor 是使用那种性质的机器。

abstract.en: Picture one small engine moving an entire field of heavy soil behind it.
abstract.cn: 想象一台小引擎把一整块沉重的土地拖在身后。

abstract.en: Think of a dog pulling a sled, then make the dog iron and the sled a plough.
abstract.cn: 想一只狗拉着雪橇，再把狗换成铁、雪橇换成犁。

abstract.en: A tractor is strength that only knows one direction: forward.
abstract.cn: 拖拉机是一种只知道一个方向的力气：向前。

examples.en: The tractor was parked behind the barn.
examples.cn: 拖拉机停在谷仓后面。

examples.en: Without a tractor the farmers would need many more hands.
examples.cn: 没有拖拉机，农夫们就需要多得多的人手。

examples.en: He learned to drive a tractor at the age of twelve.
examples.cn: 他十二岁就学会了开拖拉机。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「拽克特」——专门拽着东西往前走的那个特家伙，就是拖拉机。

root: 拉丁语 trahere（拉、拖）→ 词干 tract- + 施动后缀 -or → 拉丁形容词式 tractor（拉的东西）→ 近代英语 tractor（牵引机、拖拉机）。同族词有 traction、tract、attract、extract、contract。

sensesIntro.en: The whole entry rests on one job, pulling: the farm machine, the road tow truck, and the motor mower that drags itself forward are all names of the puller.
sensesIntro.cn: 整条词义都建立在一件事上，那就是「拉」：农田里的机器、公路上的牵引车，以及自己拖着走的割草机，都是「拉者」的称呼。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an engine with huge rear wheels dragging a plough.
core.cn: 核心意象：后轮巨大的引擎拖着犁前行。

branches.en: The machine that pulls farm tools.
branches.cn: 拖农具的机器。

branches.en: The machine that pulls trailers on roads.
branches.cn: 在公路上拖挂车的机器。

branches.en: The small motor that drags itself over grass.
branches.cn: 拖着自己在草地上走的小马达。

branches.en: The core pulling image restated.
branches.cn: 核心「拉」的意象重述。

branches.en: The same power moved off the farm.
branches.cn: 同一种动力离开了农田。

intro.en: Tractor is built on the Latin stem tract- plus the agent suffix -or, and its family spreads across prefixes such as at-, ex-, con-, de-, and sub-.
intro.cn: tractor 由拉丁词干 tract- 加施动后缀 -or 构成，其词族散布在 at-、ex-、con-、de-、sub- 等前缀上。

latinIntro.en: The Latin verb and its participle are the source of every English word given below.
latinIntro.cn: 下面的拉丁动词及其分词是以下所有英语词的来源。

items.example: The stem is shared by tractor and traction.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干被 tractor 与 traction 共享。

items.example: Tractor is the thing that pulls.
Traction is the act of pulling.
Detract means to pull value away.
Subtract means to pull away from below the total.
items.exampleCN: subtract 意为从总数中扣减。

items.example: A tractable load can be pulled along.
items.exampleCN: tractable 的负载是可以被拉动的。

definition_zh: 坑；深洞；矿井；果核；使凹陷；留下凹坑
definition_en: a deep hole in the ground, a coal mine, the hard stone inside a fruit, or to mark a surface with small hollows
core_image: 雨后的土路上，车轮把软泥压出一个深深的圆坑，里面积着浑水
scene: 雨后的土路上，一辆卡车驶过，车轮把软泥压出一个深深的坑，积水映着天光。 The truck's rear wheel dropped into a deep pit beside the road.
sceneCN: 这里是「坑、深洞」（第 1 个义项：地面向下陷出的深洞）；句意为卡车的后轮陷进了路边的深坑。画面里是那个积着浑水的圆坑。

pos.zh: 使凹陷；留下凹坑；把……放进坑里

derivatives.zh: 由 pit 与 fall 复合而成，本指陷阱，引申为「隐患；容易犯的错误」
由 pit 加 -ed 构成，形容表面布满小凹坑的
由 pit 与 stop 复合而成，指赛车中途进站加油换胎，也指长途中的短暂停留

senses.title: A deep hole in the ground
senses.definition: a deep hole in the ground, either natural or dug out by people
senses.definitionCN: 地面上的深洞，或天然形成，或由人挖出
senses.example: Rainwater had collected at the bottom of the pit.
senses.exampleCN: 雨水积在坑底。
senses.why: Old English pytt named a shaft dug down to water or to a grave, so depth and digging are built into the word rather than added later.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 pytt 本指向下挖到水层或墓穴的竖井，「往下」和「挖出来」从一开始就写在这个词里，坑的义项并不是后来才借来的比喻。

senses.title: A coal mine or its underground workings
senses.definition: a coal mine, or the shaft and tunnels through which coal is taken from the earth
senses.definitionCN: 煤矿，或从地下取煤的竖井与坑道
senses.example: His grandfather spent forty years down the pit.
senses.exampleCN: 他的祖父在矿井下干了四十年。
senses.why: A mine is only a pit enlarged and followed downward along a seam, so miners kept the plain word for the hole and let it name the whole working.
senses.whyCN: 矿井不过是被放大、并顺着煤层一路往地下延伸的坑；矿工沿用「坑」这个朴素说法，让它指整个开采系统，词义便从「洞」扩成「洞所代表的产业空间」。

senses.title: The hard stone at the centre of a fruit
senses.definition: the hard stone at the centre of a fruit such as a peach or a cherry
senses.definitionCN: 桃、樱桃等果实中心那枚坚硬的核
senses.example: She spat the cherry pit into her hand.
senses.exampleCN: 她把樱桃核吐到手里。
senses.why: A stone sits in a small hollow at the heart of the fruit, and American English took that hollow as the link, transferring the word for a pit to the hard body inside it.
senses.whyCN: 果核正嵌在果实中央一个小凹腔里，美式英语抓住这层「软东西里藏着一个小坑」的相似，把表示坑的词转到了核上，于是「地里的洞」变成了「果肉里的硬核」。

senses.title: To mark or hollow a surface
senses.definition: to make small hollows in a surface, or to become marked with such hollows
senses.definitionCN: 在表面弄出小凹坑，或变得坑坑洼洼
senses.example: Hail had pitted the roof of the old car.
senses.exampleCN: 冰雹把旧车的车顶砸出了一个个小坑。
senses.why: Once the noun names a hollow, the verb only has to name the act of producing one, and English often turns concrete nouns into verbs without adding any suffix.
senses.whyCN: 名词既然已经指一个凹下去的洞，动词就顺理成章指「造出这样的洞」；英语常把这类具体名词直接当动词用，不加词尾，于是「坑」变成了「砸出坑」。

intro.en: Pit is a Germanic word whose oldest recorded English form is pytt, and the word for a well or shaft is generally traced back to Latin puteus.
intro.cn: pit 是一个日耳曼词，英语里最早的形式写作 pytt；表示井、竖井的这个词一般认为可以上溯到拉丁语 puteus。

items.en: Puteus meant a well or a shaft dug down to water, and it is generally taken as the source of the Germanic word for a pit.
items.cn: puteus 意为水井，或向下挖到水层的竖井；一般认为它就是日耳曼语中表示「坑」的那个词的来源。

items.en: A reconstructed West Germanic form is posited as the bridge between puteus and English; it is a reconstruction, not a word found in any text.
items.cn: 学界为 puteus 与英语之间设想了一个西日耳曼语的重构形式作为桥梁；它属于重构，并非任何文本里实际出现的词。

items.en: Old English pytt meant a pit, a well or a grave, and it is recorded early both in place names and in ordinary use.
items.cn: 古英语 pytt 意为坑、井或墓穴，很早便见于地名与日常用语。

items.en: Middle English pit kept the hole and the grave, and the verb pit began to mean putting something into a hole or marking a surface with hollows.
items.cn: 中古英语 pit 保留了「坑」与「墓穴」两义，动词 pit 也开始表示把东西放进坑里，或在表面留下凹坑。

items.en: Modern English extends the word to coal mines, fruit stones and small hollows, and fixes phrases such as pit against and pit stop.
items.cn: 现代英语把词义扩展到煤矿、果核与小凹坑，并固定下 pit against 与 pit stop 这类说法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms built from the word and spellings that merely resemble it; the near-meaning group gathers words for holes, channels and mines.
note.cn: 形近组收由这个词构成的形式，以及仅仅外形相似的拼写；近义组收表示洞、沟渠与矿坑的词。

entries.definition: Marked with small hollows, or having had the stone removed, as with olives.
entries.definitionCN: 布满小凹坑的，或已经去核的，如橄榄。

entries.definition: A hidden danger or an easy mistake to make; literally a covered hole to catch animals.
entries.definitionCN: 隐藏的危险或容易犯的错误；字面上是捕捉动物用的暗坑。

entries.definition: The soft spongy tissue inside a stem or under the rind of citrus fruit; it only looks similar and has a different root.
entries.definitionCN: 植物茎内或柑橘皮下的海绵状软组织；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: A sliding part that moves up and down inside a cylinder; the spelling is close but the origin is different.
entries.definitionCN: 在气缸内上下滑动的部件；拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: An opening or hollow in a surface, the plainest word for what a pit is.
entries.definitionCN: 表面上开口或凹陷的地方，是「坑」最朴素的对应词。

entries.definition: A long narrow channel dug in the ground, usually for drainage.
entries.definitionCN: 在地上挖出的狭长沟渠，通常用于排水。

entries.definition: An excavation made to take coal or metal from the earth.
entries.definitionCN: 为开采煤或金属而挖出的矿坑。

entries.definition: A small natural depression in a surface.
entries.definitionCN: 表面上天然形成的小凹陷。

normalIntro.en: A Latin word for a well, its Germanic borrowing, an Old English noun and verb and a set of English compounds hold this word together.
normalIntro.cn: 一个表示水井的拉丁词、它在日耳曼语中的借形、古英语的名词与动词，以及一串英语复合词，共同撑起这个词。

normal.en: Puteus in Latin was a well, and the Germanic word for a pit is generally traced to it, so the oldest picture is a shaft dug down for water.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 puteus 是水井，日耳曼语里表示坑的词一般认为来自它，所以最早的画面是一口为了取水而往下挖的竖井。

normal.en: Old English pytt already covered hole, well and grave, which is why the modern word can still sound slightly grim.
normal.cn: 古英语 pytt 已经兼指洞、井与墓穴，所以今天这个词有时仍带着一点阴冷的气息。

normal.en: A coal mine is called the pit because it is simply a much larger hole followed downward along the coal seam.
normal.cn: 煤矿被称为 the pit，因为它不过是一个大得多的洞，顺着煤层一路往下延伸。

normal.en: The fruit sense works by shape: a hard stone sits in a small hollow, so the name of the hollow was transferred to the stone.
normal.cn: 果核义靠形状成立：硬核嵌在一个小凹腔里，于是凹腔的名称被转给了核本身。

normal.en: Pit against comes from setting fighting birds or dogs in a pit, while pit stop comes from the marked area where racing cars are serviced.
normal.cn: pit against 来自把斗鸟或斗犬放进坑里相斗，pit stop 则来自赛车维修所用的划定区域。

abstract.en: A pit is a shape made by absence: we name the hole, not the soil that was taken out of it.
abstract.cn: 坑是由「缺失」构成的一种形状：我们命名的是那个洞，而不是被挖走的土。

abstract.en: Every sense keeps a small enclosed hollow, whether it is a mine, a fruit stone or a pockmark on a roof.
abstract.cn: 每个义项都保留着一个被围起来的小凹腔，无论它是矿井、果核，还是车顶上的麻点。

abstract.en: The phrase pit against turns a hole in the ground into a place where two forces are made to meet.
abstract.cn: pit against 这个说法把地上的一个洞，变成了让两股力量相遇的地方。

examples.en: The car's rear wheel sank into a deep pit beside the road.
examples.cn: 汽车的后轮陷进了路边一个深坑。

examples.en: He has worked down the pit since he was eighteen.
examples.cn: 他从十八岁起就在矿井下干活。

examples.en: Hail pitted the roof of the old car.
examples.cn: 冰雹把旧车的车顶砸出了一个个小坑。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「劈特」——一铲子劈下去，地上特（别）深的一个坑；pit 就是坑与深洞。

root: 拉丁语 puteus（井、坑）一般被认为是这个日耳曼词的来源，经西日耳曼语进入古英语 pytt（坑、井、墓穴）；同族词多与「向下挖出的空洞」有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core image is a hollow dug into the ground; from it branch the mine, the fruit stone and the act of marking a surface with small hollows.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心意象是一个挖进地里的空洞；矿井、果核以及「在表面砸出小坑」的动作都从它分出来。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a round hollow pressed into wet earth, with muddy water standing at the bottom.
core.cn: 核心意象：湿泥里压出的一个圆坑，坑底积着一汪浑水。

branches.en: a wheel rut filled with muddy water
branches.cn: 积着泥水的车辙坑

branches.en: a lift cage dropping into the dark
branches.cn: 罐笼沉进黑暗的井下

branches.en: a peach cut open around its stone
branches.cn: 桃子沿核切开

branches.en: hail marking the roof of a car
branches.cn: 冰雹在车顶砸出小坑

branches.en: one hollow seen in soil, in fruit and on metal
branches.cn: 同一个凹腔，出现在土里、果肉里和金属上

intro.en: A Latin noun for a well, its Germanic borrowing, the Old English noun and verb, and a few English compounds hold the word together.
intro.cn: 表示水井的拉丁名词、它在日耳曼语中的借形、古英语的名词与动词，以及几个英语复合词，共同撑起这个词。

latinIntro.en: The ancestry is recorded through Latin puteus; the West Germanic form that carried it north is a reconstruction rather than an attested word.
latinIntro.cn: 这一支的来历可由拉丁语 puteus 追到；把它带向北方的西日耳曼语形式属于重构，而非有文本可查的词。

items.meaning: a deep hole; to make hollows

definition_zh: 宏伟的；壮丽的；极好的；出色的；慷慨的；气魄宏大的
definition_en: impressively large and beautiful, excellent of its kind, generous on a grand scale, or noble in spirit
core_image: 一座巨大的穹顶压在石柱之上，让人抬头时不自觉放慢脚步
scene: 黄昏时分，游客站在广场尽头，抬头看那座穹顶，石阶上还留着白天的余温。 The magnificent dome caught the last light and seemed to lift the whole square.
sceneCN: 这里 magnificent 是「宏伟的、壮丽的」（第 1 个义项：规模与形制令人震动）；句意为那座宏伟的穹顶接住最后的天光，仿佛把整个广场托了起来。图中可辨识物件：石阶、穹顶、广场尽头的游客。

pos.zh: 宏伟的；壮丽的；极好的；慷慨的；气魄宏大的

derivatives.zh: 由 magnificent 加 -ence 构成，义为「宏伟；壮丽」
由 magnificent 加 -ly 构成，义为「宏伟地；极出色地」

senses.title: Impressively large and beautiful
senses.definition: so large and beautifully made or placed that it fills the eye and impresses the mind
senses.definitionCN: 规模巨大、形制或位置极美，足以占满视野并震动人心
senses.example: The magnificent dome caught the last light and seemed to lift the whole square.
senses.exampleCN: 那座宏伟的穹顶接住最后的天光，仿佛把整个广场都托了起来。
senses.why: Latin magnificus joined magnus, great, to -ficus, making, so the word first praises what makes its surroundings look great.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 magnificus 把意为「大」的 magnus 与意为「使……成」的 -ficus 拼在一起，所以这个词最初赞美的是让周围显得宏大的东西。

senses.title: Excellent of its kind
senses.definition: done or made to a very high standard, so that it stands out among others of its kind
senses.definitionCN: 以极高水准完成或制成，在同类之中格外突出
senses.example: She gave a magnificent performance in the final act.
senses.exampleCN: 她在最后一幕献上了一场极为出色的演出。
senses.why: Greatness is measured by effect rather than by size, so a voice or a performance that overwhelms the audience earns the same word as a building does.
senses.whyCN: 宏大与否是看效果而不是看体积，所以一副压得住全场的好嗓子、一场压得住全场的演出，能和大建筑共用同一个词。

senses.title: Generous on a grand scale
senses.definition: giving freely and in large amounts, so that the gift itself feels splendid
senses.definitionCN: 毫不吝惜地大量给予，以至于所给之物本身就显得堂皇
senses.example: The old man made a magnificent gift to the village school.
senses.exampleCN: 那位老人给村校捐了一份极为慷慨的礼物。
senses.why: Greatness turned outward becomes generosity, and a gift given without counting the cost looks as grand as any monument.
senses.whyCN: 宏大一旦朝外转，就成了慷慨；一份不计较代价送出的礼物，看上去和任何纪念碑一样气派。

senses.title: Noble and grand in spirit
senses.definition: showing a large, forgiving or courageous spirit in a moment of action
senses.definitionCN: 在行动的一刻显出宽厚、宽容或勇敢的气度
senses.example: He offered a magnificent gesture of forgiveness to the family who had wronged him.
senses.exampleCN: 他向那个曾亏待他的家庭做出了一个气魄宏大的宽恕姿态。
senses.why: If stone and sound can be magnificent, so can a choice, and the word extends from spectacle to the moral size of a person.
senses.whyCN: 既然石头与声音可以宏伟，一个选择也可以；这个词便从场面扩展到了人精神上的分量。

intro.en: Magnificent is built from two Latin pieces meaning great and making, and it reached English through French with the sense of grandeur already attached.
intro.cn: magnificent 由两个拉丁语成分拼成，分别意为「大」与「使……成」；它带着已有的「宏大」含义经法语进入英语。

items.en: Magnus was the ordinary Latin adjective for great in size, power or rank, and it stands behind a whole family of English words.
items.cn: magnus 是拉丁语中表示体积、力量或地位之「大」的普通形容词，一整族英语词都站在它背后。

items.en: The verb facere means to make or to do, and its combining form -ficus marks whatever produces or causes something.
items.cn: 动词 facere 意为「做、造」，它的构词形式 -ficus 表示「产生、造成某物」。

items.en: Magnus plus -ficus gave magnificus, literally making great, and the word described things that enlarge the scene around them.
items.cn: magnus 加 -ficus 得到 magnificus，字面意为「使……变大」，用来形容把周围景象衬托得更大的事物。

items.en: The noun magnificentia named grandeur, and the comparative magnificentior supplied the form that passed into French and then English.
items.cn: 名词 magnificentia 指宏大、壮丽，比较级 magnificentior 提供了后来经法语进入英语的那个形式。

items.en: English borrowed magnificent in the fifteenth century and now applies it to buildings, performances, gifts and acts of spirit.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪借入 magnificent，如今把它用于建筑、演出、礼物，以及精神上的举动。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers relatives built on the Latin stem for great and making; the near group gathers adjectives that also praise scale, beauty or excellence.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁语「大」与「做」这两个词干上的同族词；近义组收同样赞美规模、美感或出色的形容词。

entries.definition: The quality of being grand and splendid.
entries.definitionCN: 宏伟；壮丽；由 magnificent 加 -ence 构成。

entries.definition: In a grand or splendid manner.
entries.definitionCN: 宏伟地；极出色地；由 magnificent 加 -ly 构成。

entries.definition: To make something look larger, from the same Latin verb for making.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物看起来更大；与 magnificent 同出拉丁语中表示「做」的动词。

entries.definition: The great size or importance of something.
entries.definitionCN: 某物的巨大或重要程度；与 magnificent 共用拉丁语 magnus（大）。

entries.definition: Magnificent in appearance or very good indeed.
entries.definitionCN: 外观壮丽的；也确实非常好的。

entries.definition: Large and impressive in scale or style.
entries.definitionCN: 规模或气派上宏大而令人印象深刻的。

entries.definition: Having a dignified, royal beauty.
entries.definitionCN: 带有庄严、王者般的美感的。

entries.definition: Impressive because of size or presence.
entries.definitionCN: 因体积或气势而令人肃然起敬的。

normalIntro.en: The word joins a Latin adjective for great to a Latin verb for making, and its family keeps returning to size, splendour and actions that enlarge the people who do them.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词把拉丁语表示「大」的形容词与表示「做」的动词拼在一起，它的同族词反复回到体积、壮丽，以及让做这件事的人显得更大的举动。

normal.en: Latin magnus means great, and -ficus comes from facere, to make, so magnificent is literally making great.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 magnus 意为「大」，-ficus 出自 facere（做），所以 magnificent 字面就是「使……宏大」。

normal.en: Magnificence adds -ence for the quality, and magnificently adds -ly for the manner of doing something.
normal.cn: magnificence 加 -ence 指性质，magnificently 加 -ly 指做事的方式。

normal.en: Magnify and magnitude share the same magnus stem, so the family keeps returning to size and greatness.
normal.cn: magnify 与 magnitude 共用 magnus 这个词干，所以这个词族一直回到体积与宏大。

normal.en: The word was borrowed through French in the fifteenth century, which is why it keeps the Latin -fic- shape.
normal.cn: 这个词在十五世纪经法语借入，所以至今保留拉丁语的 -fic- 形状。

normal.en: A magnificent view praises scale and beauty, while a magnificent gift praises generosity.
normal.cn: magnificent view 赞美规模与美，magnificent gift 赞美的则是慷慨。

abstract.en: Greatness that can be seen: the word always asks the eye to widen.
abstract.cn: 一种看得见的宏大：这个词总是要求人把眼界放宽。

abstract.en: A building and a kindness can both be magnificent, because both make the world around them look larger.
abstract.cn: 一座建筑与一份善意都可以是 magnificent，因为二者都让周围的世界显得更大。

abstract.en: The word joins great to make, a reminder that grandeur is often something done rather than owned.
abstract.cn: 这个词把「大」与「做」连在一起，提醒人：气派常常是做出来的，而不是拥有的。

examples.en: The magnificent dome caught the last light and seemed to lift the whole square.
examples.cn: 那座宏伟的穹顶接住最后的天光，仿佛把整个广场都托了起来。

examples.en: She gave a magnificent performance in the final act.
examples.cn: 她在最后一幕献上了一场极为出色的演出。

examples.en: The old man made a magnificent gift to the village school.
examples.cn: 那位老人给村校捐了一份极为慷慨的礼物。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「马格尼菲森」——马戏团的大帐篷一拉开，全场都为它的宏伟惊叹；记住 magnificent 是宏伟的、极好的。

root: 拉丁语 magnus（大的）+ -ficus（做、使……，源自 facere）→ magnificus（使显得宏大的）→ magnificentia 与比较级 magnificentior → 古法语 magnificent → 英语 magnificent。

sensesIntro.en: The core is greatness made visible; the senses then divide into imposing scale, excellent quality, lavish giving and a noble spirit.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「被看见的宏大」；义项由此分成震撼的规模、极高的水准、出手阔绰的给予，以及高尚的气度。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a vast dome resting on stone columns, making every visitor slow down and look up.
core.cn: 核心意象：一座巨大的穹顶压在石柱之上，让每个来访者都放慢脚步抬头看。

branches.en: a dome lifting above the rooftops
branches.cn: 穹顶高过一片屋脊

branches.en: a crowded hall breaking into applause
branches.cn: 满堂观众爆出掌声

branches.en: a soloist holding the last note
branches.cn: 独唱者拖住最后一个音

branches.en: a cheque handed to a village school
branches.cn: 一张支票交到村校

branches.en: an old man shaking hands after cancelling a debt
branches.cn: 老人免除债务后与人握手

intro.en: Two Latin stems, one for great and one for making, their Latin derivatives and two English endings carry magnificent from size to splendour and to generosity of spirit.
intro.cn: 两个拉丁词干，一个表示「大」，一个表示「做」，加上它们的拉丁派生词与两个英语词尾，把 magnificent 从体积带到壮丽，再带到精神上的慷慨。

latinIntro.en: Magnus, facere, magnificus and magnificentia are all recorded Latin words, and the English adjective descends from the same family through French.
latinIntro.cn: magnus、facere、magnificus 与 magnificentia 都是有记录的拉丁词，英语这个形容词经法语出自同一族。

definition_zh: 纺织品；织物；纺织原料；纺织的
definition_en: cloth made by weaving or knitting, or the material from which such cloth is made
core_image: 无数细线在织机上纵横交错，最后压成一整匹平整的布
scene: 工厂把成卷的棉纱送进织机，出来时已是一整匹布。 The mill fed rolls of cotton yarn into the loom, and a bolt of textile came out.
sceneCN: 这里指「织成的布匹」（第 1 个义项：纺织成品）；句意为工厂把成卷的棉纱送进织机，出来时已是一整匹纺织品。可辨识物件：棉纱卷、织机、布匹、传送带。

derivatives.zh: 纺织产品；纺织业（由基础词加表示复数的后缀构成，语义偏移为商品类别与行业）
纺织品设计师（由基础词与表示「设计师」的词复合，语义收窄为职业）
以纺织材料为基础的（由基础词与表示「以……为基础」的词复合，语义偏移为材料属性）
类似纺织品的（由基础词加表示「像……的」后缀构成，语义偏移为性质描述）

senses.title: Woven cloth
senses.definition: cloth produced by weaving, knitting or another fabric-making process
senses.definitionCN: 通过机织、针织或其他制布工艺生产出来的布
senses.example: A bolt of textile came out of the loom.
senses.exampleCN: 一整匹布从织机里出来。
senses.why: The word comes from a Latin verb meaning 'to weave'. A textile is literally a woven thing, so the sense begins with the finished cloth.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自一个意为「编织」的拉丁动词。纺织品字面上就是「被织成的东西」，因此词义从成品布开始。

senses.title: The textile industry
senses.definition: the industry that makes cloth, usually referred to in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 制造布料的工业，通常用复数形式指整个行业
senses.example: The town's textiles employed half its workers.
senses.exampleCN: 这座镇的纺织业雇用了半数工人。
senses.why: An industry named after its product uses the plural to mean the sector as a whole, not a pile of individual cloths.
senses.whyCN: 以产品命名的行业用复数指整个部门，而不是指一堆具体的布。

senses.title: Fibre material for cloth
senses.definition: the fibre, yarn or filament from which cloth is made
senses.definitionCN: 用来制作布料的纤维、纱线或长丝
senses.example: The lab tests textile before it reaches the loom.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室在原料上织机之前先做检测。
senses.why: Because the finished cloth and its material are stages of one process, the same noun serves for both, distinguished by context.
senses.whyCN: 成品布与原料是同一过程的不同阶段，因此同一个名词兼指两者，靠语境区分。

senses.title: Relating to cloth
senses.titleCN: 形容词义：与织物有关的
senses.definition: used before a noun to mean 'of cloth, weaving or the cloth trade'
senses.definitionCN: 用在名词前，表示「织物的、织造的或纺织业的」
senses.example: Textile exports rose for the third year.
senses.exampleCN: 纺织品出口连续第三年增长。
senses.why: As an adjective the word simply labels a field, so textile exports or textile design means the cloth sector rather than a particular cloth.
senses.whyCN: 作形容词时，这个词只是给一个领域贴标签，因此纺织品出口或纺织品设计指的是布料行业，而非某一块布。

senses.title: Industrial and technical fabrics
senses.definition: engineered fabrics made for strength, filtration, protection or other technical uses
senses.definitionCN: 为强度、过滤、防护等技术用途而设计的织物
senses.example: The car uses technical textile in its seats.
senses.exampleCN: 这辆车的座椅用了技术纺织品。
senses.why: Modern fibres can be designed for a job rather than for appearance, so the word now covers fabrics that never reach a wardrobe.
senses.whyCN: 现代纤维可以为功能而非外观来设计，因此这个词现在也涵盖根本不会进入衣柜的织物。

senses.title: Non-woven fabric
senses.definition: fabric made by bonding or felting fibres rather than by weaving them
senses.definitionCN: 通过黏合或毡合纤维、而非编织制成的布
senses.example: The mask is made of non-woven textile.
senses.exampleCN: 这只口罩由非织造布制成。
senses.why: The category expanded past its own etymology: cloth can now be made without a loom, yet it still belongs to the textile family.
senses.whyCN: 这个类别超出了自身的词源：如今不用织机也能制布，但它仍属于纺织品家族。

senses.title: Textile design as a field
senses.definition: the discipline of designing patterns, structures and surfaces for cloth
senses.definitionCN: 为布料设计图案、结构与表面的学科
senses.example: She studied textile at an art school.
senses.exampleCN: 她在艺术学校学习纺织品设计。
senses.why: Once cloth became a designed surface, the noun named a course of study and a profession, not only a material.
senses.whyCN: 当布料成为被设计的表面，这个名词就指一门课程与一种职业，而不只是材料。

senses.title: Household textile goods
senses.definition: cloth goods sold for the home, such as bedding, towels and curtains, usually in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 面向家庭销售的布制品，如床品、毛巾与窗帘，通常用复数
senses.example: The shop sells home textiles on the ground floor.
senses.exampleCN: 这家店在一层卖家用纺织品。
senses.why: Retail groups cloth by where it is used. The plural marks a product category rather than any single woven piece.
senses.whyCN: 零售业按使用场所给布料分类。复数标记的是一个商品类别，而不是某一件织物。

intro.en: Textile comes from a Latin adjective meaning 'woven', built on the verb texere 'to weave'. The same verb also gives text, texture, context and tissue. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: textile 来自一个意为「织成的」的拉丁形容词，其动词是 texere「编织」。同一个动词还给出 text、texture、context 与 tissue。年代均为约数。

items.en: Latin texere meant 'to weave, plait, construct'. A text was first something woven, and only later something written.
items.cn: 拉丁 texere 意为「编织、编结、构造」。最初 text 指织成的东西，后来才指写成的东西。

items.en: The adjective textilis 'woven, able to be woven' produced the noun textilis in later usage, and English took the adjective directly.
items.cn: 形容词 textilis 意为「织成的、可织的」，在后来的用法中产生名词形式；英语直接借入了这个形容词。

items.en: French textile mediated the word in the seventeenth century, when cloth manufacture was becoming an organised trade in Europe.
items.cn: 法语 textile 在十七世纪传递了这个词；当时布料制造在欧洲正变成有组织的行业。

items.en: With mechanised spinning and weaving, textile became the standard word for mill-made cloth and for the industry itself.
items.cn: 随着机械化纺纱与织造，textile 成为工厂制布以及整个行业的标准词。

items.en: Synthetic and non-woven fibres widened the word in the twentieth century, so it now covers fabrics that are not woven at all.
items.cn: 合成纤维与非织造纤维在二十世纪拓宽了这个词，因此它现在也涵盖根本不经编织的布。

items.en: Source uncertain: the origin of texere before Latin is unsettled, and the Indo-European root often cited for it is a reconstructed form rather than a recorded word.
items.cn: 来源不确定：texere 在拉丁语之前的来源没有定论，常被引用的印欧词根属于重构形式，而非有记录的真实词形。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same weaving root that now mean different things; group two holds everyday words for cloth.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「编织」词根、但现在意思不同的词；第二组是表示布料的日常词。

entries.definition: relating to a text or wording; it shares the weaving root but followed the written branch.
entries.definitionCN: 与文本或措辞有关的；它共享编织词根，却走了「书写」这一支。

entries.definition: the feel or arrangement of a surface; it keeps the woven image as a quality rather than an object.
entries.definitionCN: 表面的手感或结构；它把编织意象保留为一种性质，而非物件。

entries.definition: written or printed words; historically 'that which is woven', now entirely separated from cloth.
entries.definitionCN: 书写或印刷的文字；历史上意为「织成之物」，如今已与布料完全分开。

entries.definition: the words around a passage, literally 'woven together'; it belongs to the writing branch, not the cloth trade.
entries.definitionCN: 一段文字周围的词语，字面义为「织在一起」；它属于书写分支，而非纺织行业。

entries.definition: cloth or any material made by joining parts; from Latin fabrica 'workshop', it stresses manufacture rather than weaving.
entries.definitionCN: 布料或任何由部件构成的材料；来自拉丁 fabrica「作坊」，强调制造而非编织。

entries.definition: the common word for woven material; it is plainer and less industrial than textile.
entries.definitionCN: 指织物的普通词；比 textile 更朴素，也更少工业色彩。

entries.definition: any substance used to make something; it is broader than textile and says nothing about weaving.
entries.definitionCN: 用来制作某物的任何物质；比 textile 宽泛，不涉及编织。

entries.definition: cloth arranged in folds as curtains or hangings; it names a use of fabric rather than the fabric itself.
entries.definitionCN: 以褶皱形式布置成窗帘或悬挂物的布；它指布料的用途，而非布料本身。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The root means 'to weave', so textile is literally 'the woven thing'.
normal.cn: 词根意为「编织」，所以 textile 字面上就是「被织成的东西」。

normal.en: Text, texture and context come from the same verb, which is why a text can be described as woven.
normal.cn: text、texture 与 context 都出自同一个动词，这也是为什么一篇文本可以被形容为「织成」的。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the industry: textile industry, textile mill, textile production.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出行业：纺织工业、纺织厂、纺织品生产。

normal.en: The plural textiles names goods and the sector, not several separate cloths.
normal.cn: 复数形式指商品与行业部门，而不是几块分开的布。

normal.en: Technical textile shows that modern fabrics may be engineered rather than woven.
normal.cn: 技术纺织品说明现代织物可以是设计出来的，而不一定是织出来的。

abstract.en: Picture thousands of threads that only become a surface when they cross.
abstract.cn: 想象成千上万根线，只有交错之后才成为一片表面。

abstract.en: Picture a word and a cloth made by the same gesture of binding strands.
abstract.cn: 想象一个词与一块布，由同一个「把线束在一起」的动作做成。

abstract.en: Picture a material that can be flat, stiff, soft or filtering without changing its name.
abstract.cn: 想象一种材料，可以是平的、硬的、软的或用于过滤，却不必改名。

examples.en: The museum displays textile from the eighteenth-century mill.
examples.cn: 博物馆展出十八世纪工厂生产的纺织品。

examples.en: Textile workers demanded cleaner air in the spinning rooms.
examples.cn: 纺织工人要求在纺纱车间里呼吸更干净的空气。

examples.en: The designers mixed textile with recycled plastic.
examples.cn: 设计师把织物与再生塑料混用。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「特克斯太尔」—— 把特别细密的线一根根织成整匹布 → 纺织品

root: 拉丁 textilis「织成的」，来自 texere「编织、编结」；同一动词还派生 text、texture、context、tissue。texere 在拉丁语之前的来源不确定，常见印欧词根属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one process: fibres are woven into cloth, cloth becomes an industry, a material, a field of design and a retail category, and finally a family of engineered fabrics that need no loom.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一过程展开：纤维被织成布，布再成为行业、材料、设计领域与零售类别，最后成为一个无需织机的工程织物家族。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: thousands of threads crossing on a loom until they hold together as one surface.
core.cn: 核心意象：成千上万根线在织机上交错，直到合成一整片表面。

branches.en: FROM FIBRE TO CLOTH: the material and the finished cloth are two ends of one process.
branches.cn: 从纤维到布：原料与成品布是同一过程的两端。

branches.en: GOODS AND SECTOR: the plural covers both mill products and the trade that makes them.
branches.cn: 商品与行业：复数形式既涵盖工厂产品，也涵盖制造它们的行业。

branches.en: AS A LABEL: the adjective marks anything belonging to cloth or the cloth trade.
branches.cn: 作为标签：形容词标记任何属于布料或纺织业的事物。

branches.en: BEYOND WEAVING: technical and non-woven fabrics keep the family name after leaving the loom.
branches.cn: 超越编织：技术织物与非织造布在离开织机后仍保留这个家族名称。

branches.en: AS DISCIPLINE: design turns cloth into a subject with patterns, structures and training.
branches.cn: 作为学科：设计把布料变成一门有图案、结构与训练体系的科目。

intro.en: Textile is one branch of a large Latin family built on weaving. The same root reaches writing, surface feel and the surrounding words of a passage.
intro.cn: textile 是以「编织」为核心的一大型拉丁词族中的一支。同一词根还通到书写、表面手感以及一段文字周围的词语。

latinIntro.en: Latin texere gives textile, text, texture, context and tissue; the past participle textus is literally 'a woven thing'.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 texere 给出 textile、text、texture、context 与 tissue；过去分词 textus 字面义就是「织成之物」。

definition_en: a cure for an illness, or a way of dealing with a problem
core_image: 病人端起一碗苦药，喝下去之后脸色慢慢转好
scene: 山里没有医院，老人用一种草根煎水给发烧的孩子退热。 In the mountain village, the grandmother used a bitter herb as a remedy for fever.
sceneCN: 这里 remedy 是「疗法、药物」（第 1 个义项：治病的方法）；句意：在山村里，祖母用一种苦味的草药作为退烧的疗法。

senses.title: A cure for an illness
senses.definition: a medicine or treatment that cures or eases a disease or a bad condition
senses.definitionCN: 治愈或缓解疾病与不良状况的药物或治疗方法
senses.example: Honey and lemon is an old remedy for a sore throat.
senses.exampleCN: 蜂蜜柠檬是治喉咙痛的古老偏方。
senses.why: The Latin word combines re- with mederi, to heal, so the core picture is something that heals a body back.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 remedium 是「治疗的手段」，所以最核心的画面就是能让人恢复的东西。

senses.title: A way of dealing with a problem
senses.definition: an action that corrects or improves a bad situation
senses.definitionCN: 纠正或改善不良局面的行动
senses.example: There is no simple remedy for traffic in the city centre.
senses.exampleCN: 市中心的交通问题没有简单的解决办法。
senses.why: If healing can restore a body, it can also restore a situation, which gives the general sense of a fix.
senses.whyCN: 身体可以治好，坏掉的局面同样可以「治好」，词义由此扩展到一般的问题。

senses.title: A legal or official form of relief
senses.definition: a legal means by which a person can put right a wrong done to them
senses.definitionCN: 当事人用以纠正其所受侵害的法律手段
senses.example: The tenant asked the court for a remedy.
senses.exampleCN: 租客向法院请求法律救济。
senses.why: Law borrows the healing image: the court restores a wronged party the way medicine restores the sick.
senses.whyCN: 法律把受损害的一方恢复原状，思路与药物恢复病人身体完全一致。

senses.title: To put something right
senses.definition: to correct a fault or make a bad situation better
senses.definitionCN: 纠正错误，或使糟糕的局面好转
senses.example: The company must remedy the fault within thirty days.
senses.exampleCN: 公司必须在三十天内修正这个缺陷。
senses.why: The noun sense turns back into a verb, naming the act of applying the cure to a fault.
senses.whyCN: 名词义回到动词义，指把疗法施加到缺陷上的那个动作。

intro.en: Remedy comes from Latin remedium, built from re- and mederi, to heal, the same root as medicine.
intro.cn: remedy 来自拉丁语 remedium，由 re- 与 mederi「治疗」构成，与 medicine 同根。

items.en: Mederi means to heal or cure, and gives the med- family of medicine and medical.
items.cn: mederi 意为治疗、治愈，产生了 medicine 与 medical 这一组 med- 词族。

items.en: Remedium adds re- to mederi and names a means of healing.
items.cn: remedium 在 mederi 前加 re-，指治疗的手段。

items.en: Old French remedie carries both the medical and the general sense of a fix.
items.cn: 古法语 remedie 同时带有医学义与一般的「解决办法」义。

items.en: English remedy first names a medicine or a treatment.
items.cn: 英语 remedy 最初指药物或疗法。

items.en: Law adopts the word for a formal means of correcting a wrong.
items.cn: 十五世纪，法律采用这个词，指纠正侵害的正式手段。

items.en: The verb use, to remedy a fault, becomes common in official and technical writing.
items.cn: 作动词表示「补救缺陷」的用法在官方与技术文本中变得常见。

note.en: Remedy shares its root with medicine and medical, and it stands near words for cures and for fixes.
note.cn: remedy 与 medicine、medical 共享词根，与表示疗法和修补的词相邻。

normal.en: Re- plus mederi, to heal, gives something that heals back to health.
normal.cn: 前缀 re- 加 mederi「治疗」，就是把人治回健康的东西。

normal.en: Medicine and medical share the identical med- root.

root: 拉丁语 remedium，由 re-（回、再）与 mederi（治疗）构成，与 medicine、medical 同根。

sensesIntro.en: Healing a body, fixing a situation, repairing a legal wrong, and the act of putting things right all hang on one image of cure.
sensesIntro.cn: 治愈身体、修复局面、纠正法律侵害，以及「把事弄好」这个动作，都挂在同一个「治愈」的画面上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: bitter medicine taken and colour returning to the face.
core.cn: 核心意象：喝下苦药，脸色慢慢恢复血色。

branches.en: The medical cure is the oldest and most physical sense.
branches.cn: 医学上的治疗是最古老、最具体的义项。

branches.en: A broken situation can be healed too, which widens the word.
branches.cn: 破掉的局面同样可以「治」，词义由此扩大。

branches.en: The law repairs a wrong as medicine repairs a body.
branches.cn: 法律修复侵害，正如药物修复身体。

branches.en: The verb names the act of applying the cure.
branches.cn: 动词义指把疗法施加于问题的动作。

branches.en: All three noun senses depend on the same metaphor of restoration.
branches.cn: 三个名词义项都依赖同一个「恢复」的比喻。

intro.en: Remedy is a compact Latin word in which a prefix and a healing root do all the work.
intro.cn: remedy 是一个紧凑的拉丁词，前缀与表示治疗的词根承担了全部表意功能。

latinIntro.en: Latin re- adds the idea of back or again, and mederi supplies the healing, so the whole means a means of healing back.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁前缀 re- 带来「回、再」的意思，mederi 提供「治疗」，整体即「把人治回去的手段」。
